lines.label: Overhang speed
lines.tooltip: This is the speed for various overhang degrees. Overhang degrees are expressed as a percentage of line width. 0 speed means no slowing down for the overhang degree range and wall speed is used

lines.label: Bridge
lines.tooltip: Set speed for external and internal bridges

layer_height.label: Layer height
layer_height.tooltip: Slicing height for each layer. Smaller layer height means more accurate and more printing time.

initial_layer_print_height.label: Initial layer height
initial_layer_print_height.tooltip: Height of initial layer. Making initial layer height to be thick slightly can improve build plate adhesion.

line_width.label: Default
line_width.tooltip: Default line width if other line widths are set to 0. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

initial_layer_line_width.label: Initial layer
initial_layer_line_width.tooltip: Line width of initial layer. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

outer_wall_line_width.label: Outer wall
outer_wall_line_width.tooltip: Line width of outer wall. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

inner_wall_line_width.label: Inner wall
inner_wall_line_width.tooltip: Line width of inner wall. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

top_surface_line_width.label: Top surface
top_surface_line_width.tooltip: Line width for top surfaces. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

sparse_infill_line_width.label: Sparse infill
sparse_infill_line_width.tooltip: Line width of internal sparse infill. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

internal_solid_infill_line_width.label: Internal solid infill
internal_solid_infill_line_width.tooltip: Line width of internal solid infill. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

support_line_width.label: Support
support_line_width.tooltip: Line width of support. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

bridge_line_width.label: Bridge
bridge_line_width.tooltip:
Bridge line width is expressed either as an absolute value or as a percentage of the active nozzle diameter (percentages are computed from the nozzle diameter).
Recommended to use with a higher Bridge density or Bridge flow ratio.

The maximum value is 100% or the nozzle diameter.
If set to 0, bridges keep their usual width: thick bridges use the nozzle diameter, other bridges and overhang walls the line width of their feature.

seam_position.label: Seam position
seam_position.tooltip: The start position to print each part of outer wall. Back places the seam toward the back of the bed. Aligned front/left/right work like Aligned back, but bias the seam toward the front/left/right of the bed instead: hidden and low-visibility points on that side of the model are still preferred over an exposed point.

staggered_inner_seams.label: Staggered inner seams
staggered_inner_seams.tooltip: This option causes the inner seams to be shifted backwards based on their depth, forming a zigzag pattern.

seam_prefer_part_joints.label: Hide seam in part joints
seam_prefer_part_joints.tooltip: For the Aligned seam positions (Aligned, Aligned back, Aligned front, Aligned left and Aligned right): when an object is an assembly of parts, or touches another object, put the seam on the line where two parts meet, so it hides in the joint instead of on a corner elsewhere. Painted seam enforcers and blockers still take priority. Objects made of a single part are not affected.

seam_gap.label: Seam gap
seam_gap.tooltip:
In order to reduce the visibility of the seam in a closed loop extrusion, the loop is interrupted and shortened by a specified amount.
This amount can be specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the nozzle diameter. The default value for this parameter is 10%.

seam_slope_type.label: Scarf joint seam (beta)
seam_slope_type.tooltip: Use scarf joint to minimize seam visibility and increase seam strength.

seam_slope_conditional.label: Conditional scarf joint
seam_slope_conditional.tooltip: Apply scarf joints only to smooth perimeters where traditional seams do not conceal the seams at sharp corners effectively.

scarf_angle_threshold.label: Conditional angle threshold
scarf_angle_threshold.tooltip:
This option sets the threshold angle for applying a conditional scarf joint seam.
If the maximum angle within the perimeter loop exceeds this value (indicating the absence of sharp corners), a scarf joint seam will be used. The default value is 155°.

scarf_overhang_threshold.label: Conditional overhang threshold
scarf_overhang_threshold.tooltip: This option determines the overhang threshold for the application of scarf joint seams. If the unsupported portion of the perimeter is less than this threshold, scarf joint seams will be applied. The default threshold is set at 40% of the external wall's width. Due to performance considerations, the degree of overhang is estimated.

scarf_joint_speed.label: Scarf joint speed
scarf_joint_speed.tooltip: This option sets the printing speed for scarf joints. It is recommended to print scarf joints at a slow speed (less than 100 mm/s). It's also advisable to enable 'Extrusion rate smoothing' if the set speed varies significantly from the speed of the outer or inner walls. If the speed specified here is higher than the speed of the outer or inner walls, the printer will default to the slower of the two speeds. When specified as a percentage (e.g., 80%), the speed is calculated based on the respective outer or inner wall speed. The default value is set to 100%.

seam_slope_start_height.label: Scarf start height
seam_slope_start_height.tooltip:
Start height of the scarf.
This amount can be specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the current layer height. The default value for this parameter is 0.

seam_slope_entire_loop.label: Scarf around entire wall
seam_slope_entire_loop.tooltip: The scarf extends to the entire length of the wall.

seam_slope_min_length.label: Scarf length
seam_slope_min_length.tooltip: Length of the scarf. Setting this parameter to zero effectively disables the scarf.

seam_slope_steps.label: Scarf steps
seam_slope_steps.tooltip: Minimum number of segments of each scarf.

scarf_joint_flow_ratio.label: Scarf joint flow ratio
scarf_joint_flow_ratio.tooltip: This factor affects the amount of material for scarf joints.

seam_slope_inner_walls.label: Scarf joint for inner walls
seam_slope_inner_walls.tooltip: Use scarf joint for inner walls as well.

role_based_wipe_speed.label: Role base wipe speed
role_based_wipe_speed.tooltip: The wipe speed is determined by the speed of the current extrusion role. e.g. if a wipe action is executed immediately following an outer wall extrusion, the speed of the outer wall extrusion will be utilized for the wipe action.

wipe_speed.label: Wipe speed
wipe_speed.tooltip: The wipe speed is determined by the speed setting specified in this configuration. If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 80%), it will be calculated based on the travel speed setting above. The default value for this parameter is 80%.

wipe_on_loops.label: Wipe on loops
wipe_on_loops.tooltip: To minimize the visibility of the seam in a closed loop extrusion, a small inward movement is executed before the extruder leaves the loop.

wipe_inward.label: Wipe inward
wipe_inward.tooltip:
Applies only to external walls, including hole boundaries. Moves the hot nozzle toward printed inner walls during wiping to reduce reheating of freshly printed plastic and seam marks.

Especially useful at layer heights below 0.1 mm, where wipe marks are more visible.

Uses the regular wipe if no adjacent inner wall is already printed (single-wall areas or Outer/Inner wall order), or if no supported inward path can be found, for example at tight corners or seam gaps.

wipe_inward_distance.label: Wipe inward distance
wipe_inward_distance.tooltip:
The distance the wipe path is shifted away from the external perimeter, specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the actual outer-wall extrusion width.

For example, 50% shifts the path by half of the outer-wall width. The effective offset is limited by both the actual outer-wall width and the available spacing to the adjacent wall, so values above 100% or an equivalent absolute distance have no additional effect. Set to 0 to disable the offset.

wipe_before_external_loop.label: Wipe before external loop
wipe_before_external_loop.tooltip:
To minimize visibility of potential overextrusion at the start of an external perimeter when printing with Outer/Inner or Inner/Outer/Inner wall print order, the de-retraction is performed slightly on the inside from the start of the external perimeter. That way any potential over extrusion is hidden from the outside surface.

This is useful when printing with Outer/Inner or Inner/Outer/Inner wall print order as in these modes it is more likely an external perimeter is printed immediately after a de-retraction move.

slice_closing_radius.label: Slice gap closing radius
slice_closing_radius.tooltip: Cracks smaller than 2x gap closing radius are being filled during the triangle mesh slicing. The gap closing operation may reduce the final print resolution, therefore it is advisable to keep the value reasonably low.

resolution.label: Resolution
resolution.tooltip: The G-code path is generated after simplifying the contour of models to avoid too many points and G-code lines. Smaller value means higher resolution and more time to slice.

enable_arc_fitting.label: Arc fitting
enable_arc_fitting.tooltip:
Enable this to get a G-code file which has G2 and G3 moves. The fitting tolerance is same as the resolution.

Note: For Klipper machines, this option is recommended to be disabled. Klipper does not benefit from arc commands as these are split again into line segments by the firmware. This results in a reduction in surface quality as line segments are converted to arcs by the slicer and then back to line segments by the firmware.

xy_hole_compensation.label: X-Y hole compensation
xy_hole_compensation.tooltip: Holes in objects will expand or contract in the XY plane by the configured value. Positive values make holes bigger, negative values make holes smaller. This function is used to adjust sizes slightly when the objects have assembling issues.

xy_contour_compensation.label: X-Y contour compensation
xy_contour_compensation.tooltip: Contours of objects will expand or contract in the XY plane by the configured value. Positive values make contours bigger, negative values make contours smaller. This function is used to adjust sizes slightly when the objects have assembling issues.

enable_circle_compensation.label: Auto circle contour-hole compensation
enable_circle_compensation.tooltip: Bambu Studio's automatic size compensation for circular holes and circular contours. Each circle is offset by an amount computed from its diameter and the wall filament's compensation coefficients, and circles below the filament's diameter limit (50 mm by default) print their walls at the filament's compensation speed. This is separate from the fixed X-Y hole and contour compensation, which are switched off while this is on, and from polyhole conversion. Bambu Lab ships coefficients for PLA Basic, PLA CF, PET CF, PETG CF and PETG HF; other filaments use the defaults.

circle_compensation_manual_offset.label: Circle compensation offset
circle_compensation_manual_offset.tooltip: Extra offset added to the auto circle compensation, half of it on each side of the circle wall: positive values make compensated holes larger and contours smaller (a looser fit), negative values the opposite. The same arithmetic as Bambu Studio, so its projects print the same sizes.

apply_scarf_seam_on_circles.label: Scarf seam on compensated circles
apply_scarf_seam_on_circles.tooltip: Print the walls of circles compensated by the auto circle compensation with a scarf seam, for better dimensional accuracy.

elefant_foot_compensation.label: Elephant foot compensation
elefant_foot_compensation.tooltip: Shrinks the initial layer on build plate to compensate for elephant foot effect.

elefant_foot_layers_density.label: Elephant foot layers density
elefant_foot_layers_density.tooltip: Density of the internal solid infill on the elephant foot compensation layers. This value is used on the second layer; the following layers get linearly denser up to the number of layers set in "Elephant foot compensation layers". 100% disables this compensation. Not applied when printing on a raft.

elefant_foot_compensation_layers.label: Elephant foot compensation layers
elefant_foot_compensation_layers.tooltip: The number of layers on which the elephant foot compensation will be active. The first layer will be shrunk by the elephant foot compensation value, then the next layers will be linearly shrunk less, up to the layer indicated by this value.

precise_outer_wall.label: Precise wall
precise_outer_wall.tooltip: Improve shell precision by adjusting outer wall spacing. This also improves layer consistency. NOTE: This option will be ignored for outer-inner or inner-outer-inner wall sequences.

precise_z_height.label: Precise Z height
precise_z_height.tooltip: Enable this to get precise z height of object after slicing. It will get the precise object height by fine-tuning the layer heights of the last few layers. Note that this is an experimental parameter.

hole_to_polyhole.label: Convert holes to polyholes
hole_to_polyhole.tooltip:
Search for almost-circular holes that span more than one layer and convert the geometry to polyholes. Use the nozzle size and the (biggest) diameter to compute the polyhole.
See http://hydraraptor.blogspot.com/2011/02/polyholes.html

hole_to_polyhole_threshold.label: Polyhole detection margin
hole_to_polyhole_threshold.tooltip:
Maximum defection of a point to the estimated radius of the circle.
As cylinders are often exported as triangles of varying size, points may not be on the circle circumference. This setting allows you some leeway to broaden the detection.
In mm or in % of the radius.

hole_to_polyhole_max_edges.label: Maximum Polyhole edge count
hole_to_polyhole_max_edges.tooltip:
Maximum number of polyhole edges
This setting limits the amount of edges a polyhole can have

ironing_type.label: Ironing Type
ironing_type.tooltip: Ironing is using small flow to print on same height of surface again to make flat surface more smooth. This setting controls which layer being ironed

ironing_pattern.label: Ironing Pattern
ironing_pattern.tooltip: The pattern that will be used when ironing.

ironing_flow.label: Ironing flow
ironing_flow.tooltip: The amount of material to extrude during ironing. Relative to flow of normal layer height. Too high value results in overextrusion on the surface.

ironing_spacing.label: Ironing line spacing
ironing_spacing.tooltip: The distance between the lines of ironing.

ironing_inset.label: Ironing inset
ironing_inset.tooltip: The distance to keep from the edges. A value of 0 sets this to half of the nozzle diameter.

ironing_angle.label: Ironing angle offset
ironing_angle.tooltip: The angle of ironing lines offset from the top surface.

ironing_angle_fixed.label: Fixed ironing angle
ironing_angle_fixed.tooltip: Use a fixed absolute angle for ironing.

zaa_minimize_perimeter_height.label: Minimize wall height angle
zaa_minimize_perimeter_height.tooltip:
Reduce the height of top-surface perimeters to match the model edge height.
Affects perimeters with a slope less than this angle (degrees).
A reasonable value is 35. Set to 0 to disable.

zaa_min_z.label: Minimum Z height
zaa_min_z.tooltip:
Minimum Z-layer height.
Also controls the slicing plane.

zaa_dont_alternate_fill_direction.label: Don't alternate fill direction
zaa_dont_alternate_fill_direction.tooltip: Disable alternating fill direction when using Z contouring.

zaa_speed_scaling.label: Constant flow speed scaling
zaa_speed_scaling.tooltip:
Keep volumetric flow constant on contoured moves by slowing thin segments.
A contoured bead varies between the minimum Z height and the layer height, so at the role's unchanged speed the thin end is starved of material and the Z axis has least time exactly where it moves most. This scales the feed rate by (local height / layer height), so every contoured segment extrudes at the same rate the role would at the nominal layer height. Contoured segments are only ever slowed, never sped up beyond the role's speed, and never below 10 mm/s.
At 0.2 mm layers a minimum Z height of 0.08 keeps the slowdown to 2.5x; the 0.05 default asks for 4x on the thinnest segments.

wall_generator.label: Wall generator
wall_generator.tooltip: Classic wall generator produces walls with constant extrusion width and for very thin areas is used gap-fill. Arachne engine produces walls with variable extrusion width.

wall_transition_angle.label: Wall transitioning threshold angle
wall_transition_angle.tooltip: When to create transitions between even and odd numbers of walls. A wedge shape with an angle greater than this setting will not have transitions and no walls will be printed in the center to fill the remaining space. Reducing this setting reduces the number and length of these center walls, but may leave gaps or overextrude.

wall_transition_filter_deviation.label: Wall transitioning filter margin
wall_transition_filter_deviation.tooltip: Prevent transitioning back and forth between one extra wall and one less. This margin extends the range of extrusion widths which follow to [Minimum wall width - margin, 2 * Minimum wall width + margin]. Increasing this margin reduces the number of transitions, which reduces the number of extrusion starts/stops and travel time. However, large extrusion width variation can lead to under- or overextrusion problems. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter.

wall_transition_length.label: Wall transition length
wall_transition_length.tooltip: When transitioning between different numbers of walls as the part becomes thinner, a certain amount of space is allotted to split or join the wall segments. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter.

wall_distribution_count.label: Wall distribution count
wall_distribution_count.tooltip: The number of walls, counted from the center, over which the variation needs to be spread. Lower values mean that the outer walls don't change in width.

initial_layer_min_bead_width.label: First layer minimum wall width
initial_layer_min_bead_width.tooltip: The minimum wall width that should be used for the first layer is recommended to be set to the same size as the nozzle. This adjustment is expected to enhance adhesion.

min_bead_width.label: Minimum wall width
min_bead_width.tooltip: Width of the wall that will replace thin features (according to the Minimum feature size) of the model. If the Minimum wall width is thinner than the thickness of the feature, the wall will become as thick as the feature itself. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter.

min_feature_size.label: Minimum feature size
min_feature_size.tooltip: Minimum thickness of thin features. Model features that are thinner than this value will not be printed, while features thicker than than this value will be widened to the minimum wall width. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter.

min_length_factor.label: Minimum wall length
min_length_factor.tooltip:
Adjust this value to prevent short, unclosed walls from being printed, which could increase print time. Higher values remove more and longer walls.

NOTE: Bottom and top surfaces will not be affected by this value to prevent visual gaps on the outside of the model. Adjust 'One wall threshold' in the Advanced settings below to adjust the sensitivity of what is considered a top-surface. 'One wall threshold' is only visible if this setting is set above the default value of 0.5, or if single-wall top surfaces is enabled.

wall_maximum_resolution.label: Maximum wall resolution
wall_maximum_resolution.tooltip: This value determines the smallest wall line segment length in mm. The smaller you set this value, the more accurate and precise the walls will be.

wall_maximum_deviation.label: Maximum wall deviation
wall_maximum_deviation.tooltip: The maximum deviation allowed when reducing the resolution for the 'Maximum wall resolution' setting. If you increase this, the print will be less accurate, but the G-Code will be smaller. 'Maximum wall deviation' limits 'Maximum wall resolution', so if the two conflict, 'Maximum wall deviation' takes precedence.

wall_sequence.label: Walls printing order
wall_sequence.tooltip:
Print sequence of the internal (inner) and external (outer) walls.

Use Inner/Outer for best overhangs. This is because the overhanging walls can adhere to a neighbouring perimeter while printing. However, this option results in slightly reduced surface quality as the external perimeter is deformed by being squashed to the internal perimeter.

Use Inner/Outer/Inner for the best external surface finish and dimensional accuracy as the external wall is printed undisturbed from an internal perimeter. However, overhang performance will reduce as there is no internal perimeter to print the external wall against. This option requires a minimum of 3 walls to be effective as it prints the internal walls from the 3rd perimeter onwards first, then the external perimeter and, finally, the first internal perimeter. This option is recommended against the Outer/Inner option in most cases.

Use Outer/Inner for the same external wall quality and dimensional accuracy benefits of Inner/Outer/Inner option. However, the z seams will appear less consistent as the first extrusion of a new layer starts on a visible surface.

is_infill_first.label: Print infill first
is_infill_first.tooltip:
Order of wall/infill. When the tickbox is unchecked the walls are printed first, which works best in most cases.

Printing infill first may help with extreme overhangs as the walls have the neighbouring infill to adhere to. However, the infill will slightly push out the printed walls where it is attached to them, resulting in a worse external surface finish. It can also cause the infill to shine through the external surfaces of the part.

wall_direction.label: Wall loop direction
wall_direction.tooltip:
The direction which the wall loops are extruded when looking down from the top.

By default all walls are extruded in counter-clockwise, unless Reverse on even is enabled. Set this to any option other than Auto will force the wall direction regardless of the Reverse on even.

This option will be disabled if spiral vase mode is enabled.

print_flow_ratio.label: Flow ratio
print_flow_ratio.tooltip:
The material may have volumetric change after switching between molten and crystalline states. This setting changes all extrusion flow of this filament in G-code proportionally. The recommended value range is between 0.95 and 1.05. You may be able to tune this value to get a nice flat surface if there is slight overflow or underflow.

The final object flow ratio is this value multiplied by the filament flow ratio.

top_solid_infill_flow_ratio.label: Top surface flow ratio
top_solid_infill_flow_ratio.tooltip:
This factor affects the amount of material for top solid infill. You can decrease it slightly to have smooth surface finish.

The actual top surface flow used is calculated by multiplying this value with the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

bottom_solid_infill_flow_ratio.label: Bottom surface flow ratio
bottom_solid_infill_flow_ratio.tooltip:
This factor affects the amount of material for bottom solid infill.

The actual bottom solid infill flow used is calculated by multiplying this value with the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

only_one_wall_top.label: Only one wall on top surfaces
only_one_wall_top.tooltip: Use only one wall on flat top surfaces, to give more space to the top infill pattern.

min_width_top_surface.label: One wall threshold
min_width_top_surface.tooltip:
If a top surface has to be printed and it's partially covered by another layer, it won't be considered at a top layer where its width is below this value. This can be useful to not let the 'one perimeter on top' trigger on surface that should be covered only by perimeters. This value can be a mm or a % of the perimeter extrusion width.
Warning: If enabled, artifacts can be created if you have some thin features on the next layer, like letters. Set this setting to 0 to remove these artifacts.

only_one_wall_first_layer.label: Only one wall on first layer
only_one_wall_first_layer.tooltip: Use only one wall on first layer, to give more space to the bottom infill pattern.

reduce_crossing_wall.label: Avoid crossing walls
reduce_crossing_wall.tooltip: Detour and avoid to travel across wall which may cause blob on surface

max_travel_detour_distance.label: Avoid crossing walls - Max detour length
max_travel_detour_distance.tooltip: Maximum detour distance for avoiding crossing wall. Don't detour if the detour distance is larger than this value. Detour length could be specified either as an absolute value or as percentage (for example 50%) of a direct travel path. Zero to disable.

small_area_infill_flow_compensation.label: Small area flow compensation (beta)
small_area_infill_flow_compensation.tooltip: Enable flow compensation for small infill areas.

small_area_infill_flow_compensation_mode.label: Flow Compensation Model
small_area_infill_flow_compensation_mode.tooltip: Flow Compensation Model, used to adjust the flow for small infill areas. The model is expressed as a comma separated pair of values for extrusion length and flow correction factor. Each pair is on a separate line, followed by a semicolon, in the following format: "1.234, 5.678;"

bridge_flow.label: Bridge flow ratio
bridge_flow.tooltip:
This value governs the thickness of the external (visible) bridge layer.
Values above 1.0: Increase the amount of material while maintaining line spacing. This can improve line contact and strength.
Values below 1.0: Reduce the amount of material while adjusting line spacing to maintain contact. This can improve sagging.

The actual bridge flow used is calculated by multiplying this value with the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

internal_bridge_flow.label: Internal bridge flow ratio
internal_bridge_flow.tooltip:
This value governs the thickness of the internal bridge layer. This is the first layer over sparse infill so increasing it may increase strength and upper layer quality.
Values above 1.0: Increase the amount of material while maintaining line spacing. This can improve line contact and strength.
Values below 1.0: Reduce the amount of material while adjusting line spacing to maintain contact. This can improve sagging.

The actual internal bridge flow used is calculated by multiplying this value with the bridge flow ratio, the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

bridge_density.label: External bridge density
bridge_density.tooltip:
Controls the density (spacing) of external bridge lines. Default is 100%.
Theoretically, 100% means a solid bridge, but due to the tendency of bridge extrusions to sag, 100% may not be sufficient.

- Higher than 100% density (Recommended Max 125%):
  - Pros: Produces smoother bridge surfaces, as overlapping lines provide additional support during printing.
  - Cons: Can cause overextrusion, which may reduce lower and upper surface quality and increase the risk of warping.

- Lower than 100% density (Min 10%):
  - Pros: Can create a string-like first layer. Faster and with better cooling because there is more space for air to circulate around the extruded bridge.
  - Cons: May lead to sagging and poorer surface finish.

Recommended range: Minimum 10% - Maximum 125%.

internal_bridge_density.label: Internal bridge density
internal_bridge_density.tooltip:
Controls the density (spacing) of internal bridge lines. Default is 100%. 100% means a solid internal bridge.

Internal bridges act as intermediate support between sparse infill and top solid infill and can strongly affect top surface quality.

- Higher than 100% density (Recommended Max 125%):
  - Pros: Improves internal bridge strength and support under top layers, reducing sagging and improving top-surface finish.
  - Cons: Increases material use and print time; excessive density may cause overextrusion and internal stresses.

- Lower than 100% density (Min 10%):
  - Pros: Can reduce pillowing and improve cooling (more airflow through the bridge), and may speed up printing.
  - Cons: May reduce internal support, increasing the risk of sagging and top surface defects.

This option works particularly well when combined with the second internal bridge over infill option to improve bridging further before solid infill is extruded.

bridge_expansion_extra.label: Bridging infill extra expansion
bridge_expansion_extra.tooltip:
Extra distance the bridging infill grows into the surrounding area of the same part, on top of the automatic expansion.

The bridge then starts extruding over solid material before it reaches the gap, so the strand is already anchored when it begins to span. Raise this if bridges detach or curl at their ends.

With a large value the bridge takes over the whole surrounding region and the entire layer prints as one continuous bridge — useful to remove the seam artefact where the bridged area meets the supported area. There is no cap: set it as high as you need.

0 = automatic expansion only (unchanged behaviour). The automatic amount is derived from the wall count, so this setting also lets you decouple bridge anchoring from the number of walls.

thick_bridges.label: Thick external bridges
thick_bridges.tooltip:
If enabled, bridge extrusion uses a line height equal to the nozzle diameter.
This increases bridge strength and reliability, allowing longer spans, but may worsen appearance.
If disabled, bridges may look better but are generally reliable only for shorter spans.

thick_internal_bridges.label: Thick internal bridges
thick_internal_bridges.tooltip:
If enabled, internal bridge extrusion uses a line height equal to the nozzle diameter.
This increases internal bridge strength and reliability when printed over sparse infill, but may worsen appearance.
If disabled, internal bridges may look better but can be less reliable over sparse infill.

enable_extra_bridge_layer.label: Extra bridge layers (beta)
enable_extra_bridge_layer.tooltip:
This option enables the generation of an extra bridge layer over internal and/or external bridges.

Extra bridge layers help improve bridge appearance and reliability, as the solid infill is better supported. This is especially useful in fast printers, where the bridge and solid infill speeds vary greatly. The extra bridge layer results in reduced pillowing on top surfaces, as well as reduced separation of the external bridge layer from its surrounding perimeters.

It is generally recommended to set this to at least 'External bridge only', unless specific issues with the sliced model are found.

Options:
1. Disabled - does not generate second bridge layers. This is the default and is set for compatibility purposes
2. External bridge only - generates second bridge layers for external-facing bridges only. Please note that small bridges that are shorter or narrower than the set number of perimeters will be skipped as they would not benefit from a second bridge layer. If generated, the second bridge layer will be extruded parallel to the first bridge layer to reinforce the bridge strength
3. Internal bridge only - generates second bridge layers for internal bridges over sparse infill only. Please note that the internal bridges count towards the top shell layer count of your model. The second internal bridge layer will be extruded as close to perpendicular to the first as possible. If multiple regions in the same island, with varying bridge angles are present, the last region of that island will be selected as the angle reference
4. Apply to all - generates second bridge layers for both internal and external-facing bridges

dont_filter_internal_bridges.label: Filter out small internal bridges
dont_filter_internal_bridges.tooltip:
This option can help reduce pillowing on top surfaces in heavily slanted or curved models.
By default, small internal bridges are filtered out and the internal solid infill is printed directly over the sparse infill. This works well in most cases, speeding up printing without too much compromise on top surface quality.
However, in heavily slanted or curved models, especially where too low a sparse infill density is used, this may result in curling of the unsupported solid infill, causing pillowing.
Enabling limited filtering or no filtering will print internal bridge layer over slightly unsupported internal solid infill. The options below control the sensitivity of the filtering, i.e. they control where internal bridges are created:
1. Filter - enables this option. This is the default behavior and works well in most cases
2. Limited filtering - creates internal bridges on heavily slanted surfaces while avoiding unnecessary bridges. This works well for most difficult models
3. No filtering - creates internal bridges on every potential internal overhang. This option is useful for heavily slanted top surface models; however, in most cases, it creates too many unnecessary bridges

counterbore_hole_bridging.label: Bridge counterbore holes
counterbore_hole_bridging.tooltip:
This option creates bridges for counterbore holes, allowing them to be printed without support. Available modes include:
1. None: No bridge is created
2. Partially Bridged: Only a part of the unsupported area will be bridged
3. Sacrificial Layer: A full sacrificial bridge layer is created

detect_overhang_wall.label: Detect overhang wall
detect_overhang_wall.tooltip: Detect the overhang percentage relative to line width and use different speed to print. For 100%% overhang, bridge speed is used.

unsupported_wall_last.label: Print unsupported walls last
unsupported_wall_last.tooltip:
Wall loops that lie entirely in mid air are printed once something can hold them:
they are extruded after the other walls of their island, innermost first, whatever the wall order is
A loop that only the bridges of this layer can anchor waits until those bridges are printed, while a loop running alongside a supported wall keeps its place before the infill, which needs it as an anchor.

make_overhang_printable.label: Make overhangs printable
make_overhang_printable.tooltip: Modify the geometry to print overhangs without support material.

make_overhang_printable_angle.label: Make overhangs printable - Maximum angle
make_overhang_printable_angle.tooltip: Maximum angle of overhangs to allow after making more steep overhangs printable.90° will not change the model at all and allow any overhang, while 0 will replace all overhangs with conical material.

make_overhang_printable_hole_size.label: Make overhangs printable - Hole area
make_overhang_printable_hole_size.tooltip: Maximum area of a hole in the base of the model before it's filled by conical material. A value of 0 will fill all the holes in the model base.

extra_perimeters_on_overhangs.label: Extra perimeters on overhangs
extra_perimeters_on_overhangs.tooltip: Create additional perimeter paths over steep overhangs and areas where bridges cannot be anchored.

overhang_reverse.label: Reverse on even
overhang_reverse.tooltip:
Extrude perimeters that have a part over an overhang in the reverse direction on even layers. This alternating pattern can drastically improve steep overhangs.

This setting can also help reduce part warping due to the reduction of stresses in the part walls.

overhang_reverse_internal_only.label: Reverse only internal perimeters
overhang_reverse_internal_only.tooltip:
Apply the reverse perimeters logic only on internal perimeters.

This setting greatly reduces part stresses as they are now distributed in alternating directions. This should reduce part warping while also maintaining external wall quality. This feature can be very useful for warp prone material, like ABS/ASA, and also for elastic filaments, like TPU and Silk PLA. It can also help reduce warping on floating regions over supports.

For this setting to be the most effective, it is recommended to set the Reverse Threshold to 0 so that all internal walls print in alternating directions on even layers irrespective of their overhang degree.

overhang_reverse_threshold.label: Reverse threshold
overhang_reverse_threshold.tooltip:
Number of mm the overhang need to be for the reversal to be considered useful. Can be a % of the perimeter width.
Value 0 enables reversal on every even layers regardless.
When Detect overhang wall is not enabled, this option is ignored and reversal happens on every even layers regardless.

wall_loops.label: Wall loops
wall_loops.tooltip: Number of walls of every layer.

alternate_extra_wall.label: Alternate extra wall
alternate_extra_wall.tooltip:
This setting adds an extra wall to every other layer. This way the infill gets wedged vertically between the walls, resulting in stronger prints.

When this option is enabled, the ensure vertical shell thickness option needs to be disabled.

Using lightning infill together with this option is not recommended as there is limited infill to anchor the extra perimeters to.

detect_thin_wall.label: Detect thin wall
detect_thin_wall.tooltip: Detect thin wall which can't contain two line width. And use single line to print. Maybe printed not very well, because it's not closed loop.

offset_layers.label: Offset layers (experimental)
offset_layers.tooltip: Print odd-numbered walls shifted by half a layer height so layers interlock, improving layer adhesion and part strength. Experimental: works with either wall generator, and requires equal first layer and layer heights, matching top surface / outer wall line widths, and spiral vase mode off. Adaptive layer height is not supported.

top_surface_pattern.label: Top surface pattern
top_surface_pattern.tooltip: Line pattern of top surface infill.

top_surface_fill_order.label: Top surface fill order
top_surface_fill_order.tooltip:
Direction in which top surfaces are filled when using a center-based pattern (Concentric, Spiral Inset, Archimedean Chords, Octagram Spiral).
Outward starts at the center of the surface, so any excess material is pushed towards the edge where it is least visible. Inward starts at the edge and ends with the tight curves at the center.
Default uses shortest-path ordering, which may run in either direction.

top_surface_density.label: Top surface density
top_surface_density.tooltip: Density of top surface layer. A value of 100% creates a fully solid, smooth top layer. Reducing this value results in a textured top surface, according to the chosen top surface pattern. A value of 0% will result in only the walls on the top layer being created. Intended for aesthetic or functional purposes, not to fix issues such as over-extrusion.

undertop_surface_pattern.label: Undertop surface pattern
undertop_surface_pattern.tooltip: This is the line pattern for undertop surface infill.

top_shell_layers.label: Top shell layers
top_shell_layers.tooltip: This is the number of solid layers of top shell, including the top surface layer. When the thickness calculated by this value is thinner than top shell thickness, the top shell layers will be increased.

top_shell_thickness.label: Top shell thickness
top_shell_thickness.tooltip: The number of top solid layers is increased when slicing if the thickness calculated by top shell layers is thinner than this value. This can avoid having too thin shell when layer height is small. 0 means that this setting is disabled and thickness of top shell is absolutely determined by top shell layers.

top_layer_direction.label: Top layer direction
top_layer_direction.tooltip: Optional absolute angle for top-layer infill and ironing base direction. Set to -1 to use the current solid infill direction behavior.

top_surface_expansion.label: Top surface expansion
top_surface_expansion.tooltip:
Expands the top surfaces by this distance to connect distinct top surfaces and fill gaps.
Useful for cases where the top surface is interrupted by a raised feature, such as text on a plane.Expanding it removes the holes beneath these features and creates a continuous path with a better finish for printing on top.The expansion is applied to the original top surface, before any other processing such as bridging or overhang detection.

top_surface_expansion_margin.label: Top expansion wall margin
top_surface_expansion_margin.tooltip:
Using “Top surface expansion” may cause a surface that did not previously touch the model's outer walls to now do so.
This can cause contraction marks (such as the hull line) on the outer walls.
By adding a small margin, this contraction will not occur directly on the walls, thereby preventing a visible mark.

top_surface_expansion_direction.label: Top expansion direction
top_surface_expansion_direction.tooltip:
Direction in which the top surface expansion grows.
 - Inward grows into the holes and gaps left by features rising from the middle of a top surface.
 - Outward grows the outer edge of the surface, connecting surfaces separated by features that can divide a surface, such as a lattice pattern.
 - Inward and Outward does both.

top_color_penetration_layers.label: Top paint penetration layers
top_color_penetration_layers.tooltip:
How many layers deep the colour painted on a top surface is carried into the object, counting the top surface layer itself.
0 means the same depth as the top shell (top shell layers or top shell thickness, whichever is deeper).
More layers give a more solid colour, but cost more filament changes and purge.

bottom_surface_pattern.label: Bottom surface pattern
bottom_surface_pattern.tooltip: Line pattern of bottom surface infill, not bridge infill.

bottom_surface_fill_order.label: Bottom surface fill order
bottom_surface_fill_order.tooltip:
Direction in which bottom surfaces are filled when using a center-based pattern (Concentric, Spiral Inset, Archimedean Chords, Octagram Spiral).
Inward starts each surface with the wider outer curves, which improves first layer adhesion on build plates where the tight curves at the center may not stick. Outward starts at the center, pushing any excess material towards the edge.
Default uses shortest-path ordering, which may run in either direction.

bottom_surface_density.label: Bottom surface density
bottom_surface_density.tooltip:
Density of the bottom surface layer. Intended for aesthetic or functional purposes, not to fix issues such as over-extrusion.
WARNING: Lowering this value may negatively affect bed adhesion.

bottom_shell_layers.label: Bottom shell layers
bottom_shell_layers.tooltip: This is the number of solid layers of bottom shell, including the bottom surface layer. When the thickness calculated by this value is thinner than bottom shell thickness, the bottom shell layers will be increased.

bottom_shell_thickness.label: Bottom shell thickness
bottom_shell_thickness.tooltip: The number of bottom solid layers is increased when slicing if the thickness calculated by bottom shell layers is thinner than this value. This can avoid having too thin shell when layer height is small. 0 means that this setting is disabled and thickness of bottom shell is absolutely determined by bottom shell layers.

bottom_layer_direction.label: Bottom layer direction
bottom_layer_direction.tooltip: Optional absolute angle for bottom-layer infill. Set to -1 to use the current solid infill direction behavior.

center_of_surface_pattern.label: Center surface pattern on
center_of_surface_pattern.tooltip:
Chooses where the centering point of centered top/bottom surface patterns (Archimedean Chords, Octagram Spiral) is placed.
 - Each Surface: centers the pattern on every individual surface region, so each island is symmetric on its own.
 - Each Model: centers the pattern on each connected body. Parts that touch or overlap share one center; parts detached from the rest each get their own.
 - Each Assembly: uses a single shared center for the whole object or assembly.

bottom_color_penetration_layers.label: Bottom paint penetration layers
bottom_color_penetration_layers.tooltip:
How many layers deep the colour painted on a bottom surface is carried into the object, counting the bottom surface layer itself.
0 means the same depth as the bottom shell (bottom shell layers or bottom shell thickness, whichever is deeper).
More layers give a more solid colour, but cost more filament changes and purge.

top_bottom_infill_wall_overlap.label: Top/Bottom solid infill/wall overlap
top_bottom_infill_wall_overlap.tooltip: Top solid infill area is enlarged slightly to overlap with wall for better bonding and to minimize the appearance of pinholes where the top infill meets the walls. A value of 25-30% is a good starting point, minimizing the appearance of pinholes. The percentage value is relative to line width of sparse infill.

hollow_interior.label: Hollow interior
hollow_interior.tooltip: Print the part as a closed shell of even thickness with an empty cavity inside. The shell follows the surface in 3D, so sloped and curved faces get the same thickness as walls, unlike top and bottom shell layers. The cavity's ceiling is bridged. Can be set per part: a part's own setting overrides the object's.

hollow_shell_thickness.label: Hollow shell thickness
hollow_shell_thickness.tooltip: Thickness of the shell left around the cavity, measured into the part from its surface. A part has to be thicker than about twice this plus 4 mm to leave a cavity; the slicer warns about parts it could not hollow. Can be set per part.

sparse_infill_density.label: Sparse infill density
sparse_infill_density.tooltip: Density of internal sparse infill, 100% turns all sparse infill into solid infill and internal solid infill pattern will be used.

fill_multiline.label: Fill Multiline
fill_multiline.tooltip: Using multiple lines for the infill pattern, if supported by infill pattern.

sparse_infill_pattern.label: Sparse infill pattern
sparse_infill_pattern.tooltip: Line pattern for internal sparse infill.

adaptive_infill_mode.label: Adaptive density (experimental)
adaptive_infill_mode.tooltip:
Grades the Gyroid and TPMS infill inside the object: its cells grow from the surface of the object towards its center. The sparse infill density is used at the surface and the interior density at the center.
Distance warp, Smooth blend and Stepped shells follow the distance to the nearest surface, including the top and bottom, with the interior density at the point farthest from it:
 - Distance warp: one continuous pattern, stretched and sheared where the distance changes across directions, as in plates and long parts.
 - Smooth blend: the patterns of neighbouring densities blended into each other, with small loops where they meet.
 - Stepped shells: shells of the regular pattern at densities about 1.5 times apart, their lines joined along the shell boundaries.
 - Lobes: follows the 3D shape of the object, including its top and bottom. Every lobe, a part joined to the rest by a narrower neck, is graded towards its own center.
 - Normal Z, Y or X: follows the sections of the object normal to that axis, so the density does not change along it.

adaptive_infill_interior_density.label: Interior density
adaptive_infill_interior_density.tooltip: Density of the adaptive infill at the center of the object.

adaptive_infill_gradient.label: Adaptive gradient
adaptive_infill_gradient.tooltip:
How the density changes from the surface to the center of the object.
Linear: the density changes at a constant rate.
Quadratic: the density stays close to the sparse infill density near the surface and changes faster towards the center.
Exponential: the density changes quickly just below the surface and levels off towards the center.

gyroid_optimized.label: Z-buckling bias optimization (experimental)
gyroid_optimized.tooltip: Tightens the gyroid wave along the Z (vertical) axis at low infill density to shorten the effective vertical column length and improve Z-axis compression buckling resistance. Filament use is preserved. No effect at ~30% sparse infill density and above. Only applies when Sparse infill pattern is set to Gyroid.

sparse_infill_smooth_factor.label: Sparse infill smooth factor
sparse_infill_smooth_factor.tooltip: Controls how strongly sparse infill corners are rounded. 0% keeps the original sharp path, while 100% produces the largest possible curves between adjacent infill lines.

infill_direction.label: Sparse infill direction
infill_direction.tooltip: Angle for sparse infill pattern, which controls the start or main direction of line.

sparse_infill_rotate_template.label: Sparse infill rotation template
sparse_infill_rotate_template.tooltip: Rotate the sparse infill direction per layer using a template of angles. Enter comma-separated degrees (e.g., '0,30,60,90'). Angles are applied in order by layer and repeat when the list ends. Advanced syntax is supported: '+5' rotates +5° every layer; '+5#5' rotates +5° every 5 layers. See the Wiki for details. When a template is set, the standard infill direction setting is ignored. Note: some infill patterns (e.g., Gyroid) control rotation themselves; use with care.

locked_skin_infill_pattern.label: Skin infill pattern
locked_skin_infill_pattern.tooltip: Line pattern drawn in the skin band - the shell of sparse infill within "Skin infill depth" of the model surface. "Same as sparse infill" uses the sparse infill pattern, so only density and line width tell the two bands apart.

skin_infill_density.label: Skin infill density
skin_infill_density.tooltip: The portion of the model's outer surface within a certain depth range is called the skin. This parameter is used to adjust the density of this section. When two regions have the same sparse infill settings but different skin densities, this area will not be split into two separate regions. Default is as same as infill density.

locked_skeleton_infill_pattern.label: Skeleton infill pattern
locked_skeleton_infill_pattern.tooltip: Line pattern drawn in the skeleton band - everything deeper inside the model than the skin. "Same as sparse infill" uses the sparse infill pattern, so only density and line width tell the two bands apart.

skeleton_infill_density.label: Skeleton infill density
skeleton_infill_density.tooltip: The remaining part of the model contour after removing a certain depth from the surface is called the skeleton. This parameter is used to adjust the density of this section. When two regions have the same sparse infill settings but different skeleton densities, their skeleton areas will develop overlapping sections. Default is as same as infill density.

infill_lock_depth.label: Infill lock depth
infill_lock_depth.tooltip: The parameter sets the overlapping depth between the interior and skin.

skin_infill_depth.label: Skin infill depth
skin_infill_depth.tooltip: The parameter sets the depth of skin.

skin_infill_line_width.label: Skin line width
skin_infill_line_width.tooltip: Adjust the line width of the selected skin paths.

skeleton_infill_line_width.label: Skeleton line width
skeleton_infill_line_width.tooltip: Adjust the line width of the selected skeleton paths.

infill_instead_top_bottom_surfaces.label: Skin follows the surface
infill_instead_top_bottom_surfaces.tooltip: Locked Zag only. Fills the model's top and bottom surfaces with the skin band instead of solid infill, so the skin hugs the contour of the model rather than sitting in a band of uniform depth below it. Turn off for a plain depth-offset skin.

symmetric_infill_y_axis.label: Symmetric infill Y axis
symmetric_infill_y_axis.tooltip: If the model has two parts that are symmetric about the Y axis, and you want these parts to have symmetric textures, please click this option on one of the parts.

infill_complete_top.label: Fill pattern tops
infill_complete_top.tooltip: Choose this option if you want to completely fill in the tops of the infill pattern

infill_shift_step.label: Infill shift step
infill_shift_step.tooltip: This parameter adds a slight displacement to each layer of infill to create a cross texture.

lateral_lattice_angle_1.label: Lateral lattice angle 1
lateral_lattice_angle_1.tooltip: The angle of the first set of Lateral lattice elements in the Z direction. Zero is vertical.

lateral_lattice_angle_2.label: Lateral lattice angle 2
lateral_lattice_angle_2.tooltip: The angle of the second set of Lateral lattice elements in the Z direction. Zero is vertical.

infill_overhang_angle.label: Infill overhang angle
infill_overhang_angle.tooltip: The angle of the infill angled lines. 60° will result in a pure honeycomb.

lightning_overhang_angle.label: Lightning overhang angle
lightning_overhang_angle.tooltip: Maximum overhang angle for Lightning infill support propagation.

lightning_prune_angle.label: Prune angle
lightning_prune_angle.tooltip: Controls how aggressively short or unsupported Lightning branches are pruned. This angle is converted internally to a per-layer distance.

lightning_straightening_angle.label: Straightening angle
lightning_straightening_angle.tooltip: Maximum straightening angle used to simplify Lightning branches.

infill_anchor_max.label: Maximum length of the infill anchor
infill_anchor_max.tooltip:
Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. EdgeSlicer tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than this parameter is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one side and the length of the perimeter segment taken is limited to infill_anchor, but no longer than this parameter.
If set to 0, the old algorithm for infill connection will be used, it should create the same result as with 1000 & 0.

infill_anchor.label: Sparse infill anchor length
infill_anchor.tooltip:
Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. EdgeSlicer tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than infill_anchor_max is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one side and the length of the perimeter segment taken is limited to this parameter, but no longer than anchor_length_max.
Set this parameter to zero to disable anchoring perimeters connected to a single infill line.

internal_solid_infill_pattern.label: Internal solid infill pattern
internal_solid_infill_pattern.tooltip: Line pattern of internal solid infill. if the detect narrow internal solid infill be enabled, the concentric pattern will be used for the small area.

solid_infill_direction.label: Solid infill direction
solid_infill_direction.tooltip: Angle for solid infill pattern, which controls the start or main direction of line.

solid_infill_rotate_template.label: Solid infill rotation template
solid_infill_rotate_template.tooltip: This parameter adds a rotation of solid infill direction to each layer according to the specified template. The template is a comma-separated list of angles in degrees, e.g. '0,90'. The first angle is applied to the first layer, the second angle to the second layer, and so on. If there are more layers than angles, the angles will be repeated. Note that not all solid infill patterns support rotation.

gap_fill_target.label: Apply gap fill
gap_fill_target.tooltip:
Enables gap fill for the selected solid surfaces. The minimum gap length that will be filled can be controlled from the filter out tiny gaps option below.

Options:
1. Everywhere: Applies gap fill to top, bottom and internal solid surfaces for maximum strength
2. Top and Bottom surfaces: Applies gap fill to top and bottom surfaces only, balancing print speed, reducing potential over extrusion in the solid infill and making sure the top and bottom surfaces have no pinhole gaps
3. Nowhere: Disables gap fill for all solid infill areas

Note that if using the classic perimeter generator, gap fill may also be generated between perimeters, if a full width line cannot fit between them. That perimeter gap fill is not controlled by this setting.

If you would like all gap fill, including the classic perimeter generated one, removed, set the filter out tiny gaps value to a large number, like 999999.

However this is not advised, as gap fill between perimeters is contributing to the model's strength. For models where excessive gap fill is generated between perimeters, a better option would be to switch to the arachne wall generator and use this option to control whether the cosmetic top and bottom surface gap fill is generated.

filter_out_gap_fill.label: Filter out tiny gaps
filter_out_gap_fill.tooltip: Don't print gap fill with a length is smaller than the threshold specified (in mm). This setting applies to top, bottom and solid infill and, if using the classic perimeter generator, to wall gap fill.

separated_infills.label: Separated infills
separated_infills.tooltip:
Centers the internal infill of each part on itself, as if it were sliced on its own, instead of on the whole assembly. Parts that touch or overlap are treated as one body and share a center; separate parts (or distinct 3D objects) each get their own.
Useful when an assembly groups several objects that should each keep a consistent, self-centered infill.
Adaptive Cubic and Support Cubic always center each part on itself, and Lightning infill is generated for the whole object and is unaffected.

infill_wall_overlap.label: Infill/Wall overlap
infill_wall_overlap.tooltip: Infill area is enlarged slightly to overlap with wall for better bonding. The percentage value is relative to line width of sparse infill. Set this value to ~10-15% to minimize potential over extrusion and accumulation of material resulting in rough top surfaces.

align_infill_direction_to_model.label: Align infill direction to model
align_infill_direction_to_model.tooltip:
Aligns infill, bridge, ironing and surface fill directions to follow the model's orientation on the build plate.
When enabled, directions rotate with the model to maintain optimal strength characteristics.

extra_solid_infills.label: Insert solid layers
extra_solid_infills.tooltip: Insert solid infill at specific layers. Use N to insert every Nth layer, N#K to insert K consecutive solid layers every N layers (K is optional, e.g. '5#' equals '5#1'), or a comma-separated list (e.g. 1,7,9) to insert at explicit layers. Layers are 1-based.

bridge_angle.label: External bridge infill direction
bridge_angle.tooltip:
External Bridging angle override.
If left to zero, the bridging angle will be calculated automatically for each specific bridge.
Otherwise the provided angle will be used according to:
 - The absolute coordinates
 - The absolute coordinates + Model rotation: If Align infill direction to model is enabled
 - The optimal automatic angle + this value: If 'Relative Bridge Angle' is enabled

Use 180° for zero absolute angle.

internal_bridge_angle.label: Internal bridge infill direction
internal_bridge_angle.tooltip:
Internal Bridging angle override.
If left to zero, the bridging angle will be calculated automatically for each specific bridge.
Otherwise the provided angle will be used according to:
 - The absolute coordinates
 - The absolute coordinates + Model rotation: If Align infill direction to model is enabled
 - The optimal automatic angle + this value: If 'Relative Bridge Angle' is enabled

Use 180° for zero absolute angle.

relative_bridge_angle.label: Relative bridge angle
relative_bridge_angle.tooltip:
When enabled, the bridge angle values are added to the automatically calculated bridge direction instead of overriding it.
Recommended to add a small angle (<10°) to improve bridge covering in closed shapes.

minimum_sparse_infill_area.label: Minimum sparse infill threshold
minimum_sparse_infill_area.tooltip: Sparse infill area which is smaller than threshold value is replaced by internal solid infill.

infill_combination.label: Infill combination
infill_combination.tooltip: Automatically Combine sparse infill of several layers to print together to reduce time. Wall is still printed with original layer height.

infill_combination_max_layer_height.label: Infill combination - Max layer height
infill_combination_max_layer_height.tooltip:
Maximum layer height for the combined sparse infill.

Set it to 0 or 100% to use the nozzle diameter (for maximum reduction in print time) or a value of ~80% to maximize sparse infill strength.

The number of layers over which infill is combined is derived by dividing this value with the layer height and rounded down to the nearest decimal.

Use either absolute mm values (eg. 0.32mm for a 0.4mm nozzle) or % values (eg 80%). This value must not be larger than the nozzle diameter.

detect_narrow_internal_solid_infill.label: Detect narrow internal solid infill
detect_narrow_internal_solid_infill.tooltip: This option will auto-detect narrow internal solid infill areas. If enabled, the concentric pattern will be used for the area to speed up printing. Otherwise, the rectilinear pattern will be used by default.

ensure_vertical_shell_thickness.label: Ensure vertical shell thickness
ensure_vertical_shell_thickness.tooltip:
Add solid infill near sloping surfaces to guarantee the vertical shell thickness (top+bottom solid layers)
None: No solid infill will be added anywhere. Caution: Use this option carefully if your model has sloped surfaces
Critical Only: Avoid adding solid infill for walls
Moderate: Add solid infill for heavily sloping surfaces only
All: Add solid infill for all suitable sloping surfaces
Default value is All.

initial_layer_speed.label: Initial layer
initial_layer_speed.tooltip: Speed of initial layer except the solid infill part. It also applies to support, support interface and the raft base on the first layer.

initial_layer_infill_speed.label: Initial layer infill
initial_layer_infill_speed.tooltip: Speed of solid infill part of initial layer.

slow_down_layers.label: Number of slow layers
slow_down_layers.tooltip: The first few layers are printed slower than normal. The speed is gradually increased in a linear fashion over the specified number of layers.

outer_wall_speed.label: Outer wall
outer_wall_speed.tooltip: Speed of outer wall which is outermost and visible. It's used to be slower than inner wall speed to get better quality.

small_perimeter_speed.label: Small perimeters
small_perimeter_speed.tooltip: This separate setting will affect the speed of perimeters having radius <= small_perimeter_threshold (usually holes). If expressed as percentage (for example: 80%) it will be calculated on the outer wall speed setting above. Set to zero for auto.

small_perimeter_threshold.label: Small perimeters threshold
small_perimeter_threshold.tooltip: This sets the threshold for small perimeter length. Default threshold is 0mm.

internal_solid_infill_speed.label: Internal solid infill
internal_solid_infill_speed.tooltip: Speed of internal solid infill, not the top and bottom surface.

top_surface_speed.label: Top surface
top_surface_speed.tooltip: Speed of top surface infill which is solid.

gap_infill_speed.label: Gap infill
gap_infill_speed.tooltip: Speed of gap infill. Gap usually has irregular line width and should be printed more slowly.

small_support_perimeter_speed.label: Small support perimeters
small_support_perimeter_speed.tooltip: Same as "Small perimeters", but for supports. This separate setting will affect the speed of support for areas <= `small_support_perimeter_threshold`. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 80%), it will be calculated on the support or support interface speed setting above. Set to zero for auto.

small_support_perimeter_threshold.label: Small support perimeters threshold
small_support_perimeter_threshold.tooltip: This sets the threshold for small support perimeter length. The default threshold is 0mm.

enable_overhang_speed.label: Slow down for overhang
enable_overhang_speed.tooltip: Enable this option to slow printing down for different overhang degree.

slowdown_for_curled_perimeters.label: Slow down for curled perimeters
slowdown_for_curled_perimeters.tooltip:
Enable this option to slow down printing in areas where perimeters may have curled upwards. For example, additional slowdown will be applied when printing overhangs on sharp corners like the front of the Benchy hull, reducing curling which compounds over multiple layers.

It is generally recommended to have this option switched on unless your printer cooling is powerful enough or the print speed is slow enough that perimeter curling does not happen. 
If printing with a high external perimeter speed, this parameter may introduce wall artifacts when slowing down, due to the potentially large variance in print speeds causing the extruder to be unable to keep up with the requested flow change.
Root cause of these artefacts is most likely PA tuning being slightly off, especially when combined with a high PA smooth time.

Recommendations when enabling this option:
1. Reduce Pressure Advance smooth time to 0.015 - 0.02 so the extruder reacts quickly to the speed changes.
2. Increase the minimum print speeds to limit the magnitude of the slowdown and reduce the variance between fast and slow segments.
3. If artifacts still appear, enable Extrusion Rate Smoothing (ERS) to further smooth the flow transitions.

Note: When this option is enabled, overhang perimeters are treated like overhangs, meaning the overhang speed is applied even if the overhanging perimeter is part of a bridge. For example, when the perimeters are 100% overhanging, with no wall supporting them from underneath, the 100% overhang speed will be applied.

overhang_shadow_inner_wall.label: Slow down inner walls next to overhangs
overhang_shadow_inner_wall.tooltip:
Give the inner wall a share of the slowdown and fan its overhanging neighbour gets.

The outer wall of an overhang is printed onto the inner wall next to it, and that inner wall went down at full speed a few seconds earlier because it is itself supported. This makes the anchor as careful as the wall it has to hold up.

Costs nothing away from an overhang: a wall with solid material under it is graded the same either way. Requires 'Slow down for overhang', and has no effect when walls are printed outer wall first.

overhang_shadow_speed_ratio.label: Inner wall slowdown
overhang_shadow_speed_ratio.tooltip:
How much of the neighbouring wall's treatment this wall borrows. 100% grades the inner wall exactly as if it were the overhanging wall itself, which also brings the overhang fan with it. 50% takes it halfway. 0% disables the effect.

The default of 30% is deliberately gentle: enough to make the anchor more likely to be there, without a speed change large enough to show on the wall.

overhang_shadow_distance.label: Inner wall reach
overhang_shadow_distance.tooltip:
How far outwards to look for the wall being mirrored, as a percentage of line width. 100% is the wall immediately next to this one. Larger values mirror something further out, so the slowdown reaches deeper into the walls.

The default of 200% looks two line widths out, which catches the overhang even where it starts a little beyond the neighbouring wall.

bridge_speed.label: External
bridge_speed.tooltip:
Speed of the externally visible bridge extrusions.

In addition, if Slow down for curled perimeters is disabled or Classic overhang mode is enabled, it will be the print speed of overhang walls that are supported by less than 13%, whether they are part of a bridge or an overhang.

internal_bridge_speed.label: Internal
internal_bridge_speed.tooltip: Speed of internal bridges. If the value is expressed as a percentage, it will be calculated based on the bridge_speed. Default value is 150%.

layer_time_speed_smoothing.label: Layer time speed smoothing
layer_time_speed_smoothing.tooltip:
Limit how much estimated print time may jump from one layer to the next, which otherwise shows up as banding on glossy and high-shrinkage filaments.

Off leaves speeds unchanged.
Speed up (exclude outer walls) shortens long layers so they sit inside the neighbour variation band, without touching outer-wall feedrates.
Speed up (all) does the same for every extrusion.
Slow down lengthens short layers instead (optional; similar in spirit to Bambu Studio's layer-time smoothing, but a separate Edge option).

layer_time_speed_max_variation.label: Max layer time variation
layer_time_speed_max_variation.tooltip: Maximum allowed relative change of estimated print time between adjacent layers. At 25%, a neighbour may be at most 25% shorter than a layer (the longer layer is at most 1 / 0.75 times the shorter). Smaller values produce a gentler ramp and cost more time (slow down) or more speed-up of the long layers.

layer_time_speed_max_speedup.label: Max speed-up
layer_time_speed_max_speedup.tooltip: Cap on how much a single long layer may be sped up (Modes Speed up). 100% means the layer may print at most twice as fast (time may be halved). Short layers are never lengthened.

layer_time_speed_max_slowdown.label: Max slowdown
layer_time_speed_max_slowdown.tooltip: Cap on how much a single short layer may be slowed down (Slow down mode). 200% means the layer may take up to three times as long.

layer_time_speed_max_time_increase.label: Max print time increase
layer_time_speed_max_time_increase.tooltip: Cap on the growth of the summed layer times (Slow down mode). If the variation limit would exceed this budget, the allowed variation is relaxed until the increase fits.

layer_time_speed_slowdown_scope.label: Slowdown scope
layer_time_speed_slowdown_scope.tooltip: Which extrusions Slow down mode may stretch. Exclude outer walls keeps outer-wall speed and gloss unchanged and only lengthens inner walls, infill and other internal extrusions. This is an apply-side choice; the time solver itself is extrusion-agnostic.

min_layer_time_pause.label: Minimum layer time (pause)
min_layer_time_pause.tooltip: If a layer still takes less than this after the filament's cooling slowdown, the head retracts, lifts, parks and waits for the rest of the time with the fan running, then carries on. For tiny layers such as thin spikes. Not on the first layer or in spiral vase mode. 0 turns it off.

min_layer_time_pause_park.label: Pause position
min_layer_time_pause_park.tooltip: Where the head waits during a minimum layer time pause. Away from the print: the nearest free bed edge or corner, clear of the objects, the prime tower and excluded areas (beside the current object when printing by object). Next to the prime tower: beside the tower, or away from the print without one. Custom: the X/Y below.

min_layer_time_pause_park_x.label: Pause position X
min_layer_time_pause_park_x.tooltip: X of the custom pause position, in bed coordinates.

min_layer_time_pause_park_y.label: Pause position Y
min_layer_time_pause_park_y.tooltip: Y of the custom pause position, in bed coordinates.

travel_speed.label: Travel
travel_speed.tooltip: Speed of travel which is faster and without extrusion.

default_acceleration.label: Normal printing
default_acceleration.tooltip: The default acceleration of both normal printing and travel except initial layer.

outer_wall_acceleration.label: Outer wall
outer_wall_acceleration.tooltip: Acceleration of outer wall. Using a lower value can improve quality.

bridge_acceleration.label: Bridge
bridge_acceleration.tooltip: Acceleration of bridges. If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 50%), it will be calculated based on the outer wall acceleration.

sparse_infill_acceleration.label: Sparse infill
sparse_infill_acceleration.tooltip: Acceleration of sparse infill. If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 100%), it will be calculated based on the default acceleration.

internal_solid_infill_acceleration.label: Internal solid infill
internal_solid_infill_acceleration.tooltip: Acceleration of internal solid infill. If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 100%), it will be calculated based on the default acceleration.

initial_layer_acceleration.label: Initial layer
initial_layer_acceleration.tooltip: Acceleration of initial layer. Using a lower value can improve build plate adhesion.

first_layer_travel_acceleration.label: First layer travel
first_layer_travel_acceleration.tooltip: Acceleration of travel moves on the first layer. If expressed as a percentage (e.g. 50%), it is calculated over the travel acceleration. 0 means first layer travels use the initial layer acceleration.

initial_layer_travel_acceleration.label: Initial layer travel
initial_layer_travel_acceleration.tooltip: The acceleration of travel of initial layer. 0 means First layer travel (above) decides.

top_surface_acceleration.label: Top surface
top_surface_acceleration.tooltip: Acceleration of top surface infill. Using a lower value may improve top surface quality.

accel_to_decel_enable.label: Enable accel_to_decel
accel_to_decel_enable.tooltip: Klipper's max_accel_to_decel will be adjusted automatically. The value is sent both as ACCEL_TO_DECEL and as the equivalent MINIMUM_CRUISE_RATIO (1 - accel_to_decel factor), which replaced it in newer Klipper and overrides minimum_cruise_ratio in printer.cfg.

accel_to_decel_factor.label: accel_to_decel
accel_to_decel_factor.tooltip: Klipper's max_accel_to_decel will be adjusted to this %% of acceleration. Newer Klipper gets it as minimum_cruise_ratio = 1 - this value (50%% sends ACCEL_TO_DECEL = half the acceleration and MINIMUM_CRUISE_RATIO=0.5).

default_junction_deviation.label: Junction Deviation
default_junction_deviation.tooltip: Marlin Firmware Junction Deviation (replaces the traditional XY Jerk setting).

first_layer_travel_jerk.label: First layer travel
first_layer_travel_jerk.tooltip: Jerk of travel moves on the first layer. If expressed as a percentage (e.g. 50%), it is calculated over the travel jerk. 0 means first layer travels use the initial layer jerk.

max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope.label: Extrusion rate smoothing
max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope.tooltip:
This parameter smooths out sudden extrusion rate changes that happen when the printer transitions from printing a high flow (high speed/larger width) extrusion to a lower flow (lower speed/smaller width) extrusion and vice versa.

It defines the maximum rate by which the extruded volumetric flow in mm³/s can change over time. Higher values mean higher extrusion rate changes are allowed, resulting in faster speed transitions.

A value of 0 disables the feature.

For a high speed, high flow direct drive printer (like the Bambu lab or Voron) this value is usually not needed. However it can provide some marginal benefit in certain cases where feature speeds vary greatly. For example, when there are aggressive slowdowns due to overhangs. In these cases a high value of around 300-350 mm³/s² is recommended as this allows for just enough smoothing to assist pressure advance achieve a smoother flow transition.

For slower printers without pressure advance, the value should be set much lower. A value of 10-15 mm³/s² is a good starting point for direct drive extruders and 5-10 mm³/s² for Bowden style.

This feature is known as Pressure Equalizer in Prusa slicer.

Note: this parameter disables arc fitting.

max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_segm.label: Smoothing segment length
max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_segm.tooltip:
A lower value results in smoother extrusion rate transitions. However, this results in a significantly larger G-code file and more instructions for the printer to process.

Default value of 3 works well for most cases. If your printer is stuttering, increase this value to reduce the number of adjustments made.

Allowed values: 0.5-5

extrusion_rate_smoothing_external_perime.label: Apply only on external features
extrusion_rate_smoothing_external_perime.tooltip: Applies extrusion rate smoothing only on external perimeters and overhangs. This can help reduce artefacts due to sharp speed transitions on externally visible overhangs without impacting the print speed of features that will not be visible to the user.

support_type.label: Type
support_type.tooltip: Normal (auto) and Tree (auto) are used to generate support automatically. If Normal (manual) or Tree (manual) is selected, only support enforcers are generated.

support_style.label: Style
support_style.tooltip:
Style and shape of the support. For normal support, projecting the supports into a regular grid will create more stable supports (default), while snug support towers will save material and reduce object scarring.
For tree support, slim and organic style will merge branches more aggressively and save a lot of material (default organic), while hybrid style will create similar structure to normal support under large flat overhangs.

support_threshold_angle.label: Threshold angle
support_threshold_angle.tooltip: Support will be generated for overhangs whose slope angle is below the threshold.

support_threshold_overlap.label: Threshold overlap
support_threshold_overlap.tooltip: If threshold angle is zero, support will be generated for overhangs whose overlap is below the threshold. The smaller this value is, the steeper the overhang that can be printed without support.

raft_first_layer_density.label: Initial layer density
raft_first_layer_density.tooltip: Density of the first raft or support layer.

raft_first_layer_expansion.label: Initial layer expansion
raft_first_layer_expansion.tooltip: Expand the first raft or support layer to improve bed plate adhesion.

support_on_build_plate_only.label: On build plate only
support_on_build_plate_only.tooltip: Don't create support on model surface, only on build plate.

support_critical_regions_only.label: Support critical regions only
support_critical_regions_only.tooltip: Only create support for critical regions including sharp tail, cantilever, etc.

support_remove_small_overhang.label: Remove small overhangs
support_remove_small_overhang.tooltip: Remove small overhangs that possibly need no supports.

raft_layers.label: Raft layers
raft_layers.tooltip: Object will be raised by this number of support layers. Use this function to avoid warping when printing ABS.

raft_contact_distance.label: Raft contact Z distance
raft_contact_distance.tooltip: Z gap between raft and object. If Support Top Z Distance is 0, this value is ignored and the object is printed in direct contact with the raft (no gap).

raft_expansion.label: Raft expansion
raft_expansion.tooltip: Expand all raft layers in XY plane.

support_filament.label: Support/raft base
support_filament.tooltip: Filament to print support base and raft. "Default" means no specific filament for support and current filament is used.

support_interface_filament.label: Support/raft interface
support_interface_filament.tooltip: Filament to print support interface. "Default" means no specific filament for support interface and current filament is used.

support_filament_matching.label: Support Filament Matching
