filament_max_volumetric_speed.label: Max volumetric speed
filament_max_volumetric_speed.tooltip: This setting stands for how much volume of filament can be melted and extruded per second. Printing speed is limited by max volumetric speed, in case of too high and unreasonable speed setting. Can't be zero.

close_fan_the_first_x_layers.label: No cooling for the first
close_fan_the_first_x_layers.tooltip: Turn off all cooling fans for the first few layers. This can be used to improve build plate adhesion.

initial_layer_fan_speed.label: First layer fan speed
initial_layer_fan_speed.tooltip:
Sets an exact fan speed for the first layer, overriding all other cooling settings. Useful for protecting 3D-printed toolhead parts (e.g. Voron-style ABS/ASA ducts) from a hot bed. A small amount of airflow cools the ducts down, without using full cooling that may in certain conditions hurt first-layer adhesion.
From the second layer onwards, normal cooling resumes.
If "Full fan speed at layer" is also set, the fan ramps smoothly from this value on the first layer up to your target by the chosen layer.
Only available when "No cooling for the first" is 0.
Set to -1 to disable it.

full_fan_speed_layer.label: Full fan speed at layer
full_fan_speed_layer.tooltip: Fan speed will be ramped up linearly from zero at layer "close_fan_the_first_x_layers" to maximum at layer "full_fan_speed_layer". "full_fan_speed_layer" will be ignored if lower than "close_fan_the_first_x_layers", in which case the fan will be running at maximum allowed speed at layer "close_fan_the_first_x_layers" + 1.

fan_min_speed.label: Fan speed
fan_min_speed.tooltip: Minimum speed for part cooling fan.

fan_cooling_layer_time.label: Layer time
fan_cooling_layer_time.tooltip: Part cooling fan will be enabled for layers of which estimated time is shorter than this value. Fan speed is interpolated between the minimum and maximum fan speeds according to layer printing time.

fan_max_speed.label: Fan speed
fan_max_speed.tooltip: Part cooling fan speed may be increased when auto cooling is enabled. This is the maximum speed for the part cooling fan.

slow_down_layer_time.label: Layer time
slow_down_layer_time.tooltip: The printing speed in exported G-code will be slowed down when the estimated layer time is shorter than this value in order to get better cooling for these layers.

reduce_fan_stop_start_freq.label: Keep fan always on
reduce_fan_stop_start_freq.tooltip: Enabling this setting means that the part cooling fan will never stop completely and will run at least at minimum speed to reduce the frequency of starting and stopping.

slow_down_for_layer_cooling.label: Slow printing down for better layer cooling
slow_down_for_layer_cooling.tooltip: Enable this option to slow printing speed down to make the final layer time not shorter than the layer time threshold in "Max fan speed threshold", so that layer can be cooled for longer time. This can improve the cooling quality for needle and small details.

dont_slow_down_outer_wall.label: Don't slow down outer walls
dont_slow_down_outer_wall.tooltip:
If enabled, this setting will ensure external perimeters are not slowed down to meet the minimum layer time. This is particularly helpful in the below scenarios:
1. To avoid changes in shine when printing glossy filaments
2. To avoid changes in external wall speed which may create slight wall artifacts that appear like Z banding
3. To avoid printing at speeds which cause VFAs (fine artifacts) on the external walls

slow_down_min_speed.label: Min print speed
slow_down_min_speed.tooltip: The minimum print speed to which the printer slows down to maintain the minimum layer time defined above when the slowdown for better layer cooling is enabled.

enable_overhang_bridge_fan.label: Force cooling for overhangs and bridges
enable_overhang_bridge_fan.tooltip: Enable this option to allow adjustment of the part cooling fan speed for specifically for overhangs, internal and external bridges. Setting the fan speed specifically for these features can improve overall print quality and reduce warping.

overhang_fan_threshold.label: Overhang cooling activation threshold
overhang_fan_threshold.tooltip: When the overhang exceeds this specified threshold, force the cooling fan to run at the 'Overhang Fan Speed' set below. This threshold is expressed as a percentage, indicating the portion of each line's width that is unsupported by the layer beneath it. Setting this value to 0% forces the cooling fan to run for all outer walls, regardless of the overhang degree.

overhang_fan_speed.label: Overhangs and external bridges fan speed
overhang_fan_speed.tooltip:
Use this part cooling fan speed when printing bridges or overhang walls with an overhang threshold that exceeds the value set in the 'Overhangs cooling threshold' parameter above. Increasing the cooling specifically for overhangs and bridges can improve the overall print quality of these features.

Please note, this fan speed is clamped on the lower end by the minimum fan speed threshold set above. It is also adjusted upwards up to the maximum fan speed threshold when the minimum layer time threshold is not met.

internal_bridge_fan_speed.label: Internal bridges fan speed
internal_bridge_fan_speed.tooltip:
The part cooling fan speed used for all internal bridges. Set to -1 to use the overhang fan speed settings instead.

Reducing the internal bridges fan speed, compared to your regular fan speed, can help reduce part warping due to excessive cooling applied over a large surface for a prolonged period of time.

support_material_interface_fan_speed.label: Support interface fan speed
support_material_interface_fan_speed.tooltip:
This part cooling fan speed is applied when printing support interfaces. Setting this parameter to a higher than regular speed reduces the layer binding strength between supports and the supported part, making them easier to separate.
Set to -1 to disable it.
This setting is overridden by disable_fan_first_layers.

ironing_fan_speed.label: Ironing fan speed
ironing_fan_speed.tooltip:
This part cooling fan speed is applied when ironing. Setting this parameter to a lower than regular speed reduces possible nozzle clogging due to the low volumetric flow rate, making the interface smoother.
Set to -1 to disable it.

additional_cooling_fan_speed.label: Fan speed
additional_cooling_fan_speed.tooltip:
Speed of auxiliary part cooling fan. Auxiliary fan will run at this speed during printing except the first several layers which is defined by no cooling layers.
Please enable auxiliary_fan in printer settings to use this feature. G-code command: M106 P2 S(0-255)

activate_air_filtration.label: Activate air filtration
activate_air_filtration.tooltip: Activate for better air filtration. G-code command: M106 P3 S(0-255)

activate_air_filtration_during_print.label: During print
activate_air_filtration_during_print.tooltip: Enable this to override the fan speed set in custom G-code during print.

during_print_exhaust_fan_speed.label: Fan speed
during_print_exhaust_fan_speed.tooltip: Speed of exhaust fan during printing. This speed will override the speed in filament custom G-code.

activate_air_filtration_on_completion.label: On completion
activate_air_filtration_on_completion.tooltip: Enable this to override the fan speed set in custom G-code after print completion.

complete_print_exhaust_fan_speed.label: Fan speed
complete_print_exhaust_fan_speed.tooltip: Speed of exhaust fan after printing completes.

filament_retraction_length.label: Length
filament_retraction_length.tooltip: Some amount of material in extruder is pulled back to avoid ooze during long travel. Set zero to disable retraction.

filament_z_hop.label: Z-hop height
filament_z_hop.tooltip: Whenever the retraction is done, the nozzle is lifted a little to create clearance between nozzle and the print. It prevents nozzle from hitting the print when travel move. Using spiral lines to lift Z can prevent stringing.

filament_retract_lift_above.label: Only lift Z above
filament_retract_lift_above.tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place above the specified absolute Z.

filament_retract_lift_below.label: Only lift Z below
filament_retract_lift_below.tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place below the specified absolute Z.

filament_retract_lift_enforce.label: On surfaces
filament_retract_lift_enforce.tooltip: Enforce Z-Hop behavior. This setting is impacted by the above settings (Only lift Z above/below).

filament_retraction_speed.label: Retraction Speed
filament_retraction_speed.tooltip: Speed for retracting filament from the nozzle.

filament_deretraction_speed.label: De-retraction Speed
filament_deretraction_speed.tooltip: Speed for reloading filament into the nozzle. Zero means same speed of retraction.

filament_retract_restart_extra.label: Extra length on restart
filament_retract_restart_extra.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after the travel move, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament. This setting is rarely needed.

filament_retraction_minimum_travel.label: Travel distance threshold
filament_retraction_minimum_travel.tooltip: Only trigger retraction when the travel distance is longer than this threshold.

filament_retract_when_changing_layer.label: Retract when change layer
filament_retract_when_changing_layer.tooltip: Force a retraction when changes layer.

filament_wipe.label: Wipe while retracting
filament_wipe.tooltip: Move nozzle along the last extrusion path when retracting to clean any leaked material on the nozzle. This can minimize blobs when printing a new part after traveling.

filament_wipe_distance.label: Wipe Distance
filament_wipe_distance.tooltip:
Describe how long the nozzle will move along the last path when retracting.

Depending on how long the wipe operation lasts, how fast and long the extruder/filament retraction settings are, a retraction move may be needed to retract the remaining filament.

Setting a value in the retract amount before wipe setting below will perform any excess retraction before the wipe, else it will be performed after.

filament_retract_before_wipe.label: Retract amount before wipe
filament_retract_before_wipe.tooltip: The length of fast retraction before wipe, relative to retraction length.

filament_retract_after_wipe.label: Retract amount after wipe
filament_retract_after_wipe.tooltip:
The length of fast retraction after wipe, relative to retraction length.
The value will be clamped by 100% minus the retract amount before the wipe value.

filament_long_retractions_when_cut.label: Long retraction when cut (beta)
filament_long_retractions_when_cut.tooltip: Experimental feature: Retracting and cutting off the filament at a longer distance during changes to minimize purge. While this reduces flush significantly, it may also raise the risk of nozzle clogs or other printing problems.

filament_retraction_distances_when_cut.label: Retraction distance when cut
filament_retraction_distances_when_cut.tooltip: Experimental feature: Retraction length before cutting off during filament change. Set zero to disable the long retraction.

filament_retract_restart_extra_toolchang.label: Extra length on restart
filament_retract_restart_extra_toolchang.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after changing tool, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament.

filament_ironing_flow.label: Ironing flow
filament_ironing_flow.tooltip: Filament-specific override for ironing flow. This allows you to customize the ironing flow for each filament type. Too high value results in overextrusion on the surface.

filament_ironing_spacing.label: Ironing line spacing
filament_ironing_spacing.tooltip: Filament-specific override for ironing line spacing. This allows you to customize the spacing between ironing lines for each filament type.

filament_ironing_inset.label: Ironing inset
filament_ironing_inset.tooltip: Filament-specific override for ironing inset. This allows you to customize the distance to keep from the edges when ironing for each filament type.

filament_ironing_speed.label: Ironing speed
filament_ironing_speed.tooltip: Filament-specific override for ironing speed. This allows you to customize the print speed of ironing lines for each filament type.

filament_start_gcode.label: Start G-code
filament_start_gcode.tooltip: Start G-code when starting the printing of this filament.

filament_change_extrusion_role_gcode.label: Change extrusion role G-code (filament)
filament_change_extrusion_role_gcode.tooltip: This G-code is inserted when the extrusion role is changed for the active filament.

filament_end_gcode.label: End G-code
filament_end_gcode.tooltip: End G-code when finishing the printing of this filament.

filament_minimal_purge_on_wipe_tower.label: Minimal purge on wipe tower
filament_minimal_purge_on_wipe_tower.tooltip: After a tool change, the exact position of the newly loaded filament inside the nozzle may not be known, and the filament pressure is likely not yet stable. Before purging the print head into an infill or a sacrificial object, EdgeSlicer will always prime this amount of material into the wipe tower to produce successive infill or sacrificial object extrusions reliably.

filament_tower_interface_print_temp.label: Tower interface temperature
filament_tower_interface_print_temp.tooltip: Nozzle temperature this filament is purged at on a prime tower interface, used by "Heat up for tower interfaces" (process setting). -1 uses the top of the recommended nozzle temperature range.

filament_tower_interface_pre_extrusion_d.label: Tower interface run-in distance
filament_tower_interface_pre_extrusion_d.tooltip: How far outside the prime tower this filament's purge starts at a tower interface, used by "Run in from outside the tower" (process setting). The prime tower's reserved area grows by this distance.

filament_tower_interface_pre_extrusion_l.label: Tower interface extra prime length
filament_tower_interface_pre_extrusion_l.tooltip: Filament pushed through the nozzle before this filament's purge at a tower interface, used by "Extra prime at tower interfaces" (process setting). 2 mm are always added, as in Bambu Studio.

filament_loading_speed_start.label: Loading speed at the start
filament_loading_speed_start.tooltip: Speed used at the very beginning of loading phase.

filament_loading_speed.label: Loading speed
filament_loading_speed.tooltip: Speed used for loading the filament on the wipe tower.

filament_unloading_speed_start.label: Unloading speed at the start
filament_unloading_speed_start.tooltip: Speed used for unloading the tip of the filament immediately after ramming.

filament_unloading_speed.label: Unloading speed
filament_unloading_speed.tooltip: Speed used for unloading the filament on the wipe tower (does not affect initial part of unloading just after ramming).

filament_toolchange_delay.label: Delay after unloading
filament_toolchange_delay.tooltip: Time to wait after the filament is unloaded. May help to get reliable tool changes with flexible materials that may need more time to shrink to original dimensions.

filament_cooling_moves.label: Number of cooling moves
filament_cooling_moves.tooltip: Filament is cooled by being moved back and forth in the cooling tubes. Specify desired number of these moves.

filament_cooling_initial_speed.label: Speed of the first cooling move
filament_cooling_initial_speed.tooltip: Cooling moves are gradually accelerating beginning at this speed.

filament_cooling_final_speed.label: Speed of the last cooling move
filament_cooling_final_speed.tooltip: Cooling moves are gradually accelerating towards this speed.

filament_stamping_distance.label: Stamping distance measured from the center of the cooling tube
filament_stamping_distance.tooltip: If set to non-zero value, filament is moved toward the nozzle between the individual cooling moves ("stamping"). This option configures how long this movement should be before the filament is retracted again.

filament_ramming_parameters.label: Ramming parameters
filament_ramming_parameters.tooltip: This string is edited by RammingDialog and contains ramming specific parameters.

filament_multitool_ramming.label: Enable ramming for multi-tool setups
filament_multitool_ramming.tooltip: Perform ramming when using multi-tool printer (i.e. when the 'Single Extruder Multimaterial' in Printer Settings is unchecked). When checked, a small amount of filament is rapidly extruded on the wipe tower just before the tool change. This option is only used when the wipe tower is enabled.

filament_multitool_ramming_volume.label: Multi-tool ramming volume
filament_multitool_ramming_volume.tooltip: The volume to be rammed before the tool change.

filament_multitool_ramming_flow.label: Multi-tool ramming flow
filament_multitool_ramming_flow.tooltip: Flow used for ramming the filament before the tool change.

filament_flush_temp.label: Flush temperature
filament_flush_temp.tooltip: temperature when flushing filament. 0 indicates the upper bound of the recommended nozzle temperature range

filament_flush_temp_fast.label: Flush temperature
filament_flush_temp_fast.tooltip: Flush temperature used in fast purge mode.

filament_flush_volumetric_speed.label: Flush volumetric speed
filament_flush_volumetric_speed.tooltip: Volumetric speed when flushing filament. 0 indicates the max volumetric speed

long_retractions_when_ec.label: Long retraction when extruder change
long_retractions_when_ec.tooltip: Experimental feature: perform a long retraction when the printer switches to the other extruder, so the idle filament is parked instead of being fully unloaded.

retraction_distances_when_ec.label: Retraction distance when extruder change
retraction_distances_when_ec.tooltip: Experimental feature: retraction length used when the printer switches to the other extruder.

compatible_printers_condition.label: Condition
compatible_printers_condition.tooltip: A boolean expression using the configuration values of an active printer profile. If this expression evaluates to true, this profile is considered compatible with the active printer profile.

compatible_prints_condition.label: Condition
compatible_prints_condition.tooltip: A boolean expression using the configuration values of an active print profile. If this expression evaluates to true, this profile is considered compatible with the active print profile.

filament_notes.label: Filament notes
filament_notes.tooltip: You can put your notes regarding the filament here.

lines.label: Frequency
lines.tooltip: The frequency of the anti-vibration signal will correspond to the natural frequency of the frame.

lines.label: Damping
lines.tooltip: Damping ratio for the input shaping filter.

bed_exclude_area.label: Bed exclude area
bed_exclude_area.tooltip: Unprintable area in XY plane. For example, X1 Series printers use the front left corner to cut filament during filament change. The area is expressed as polygon by points in following format: "XxY, XxY, ..."

printable_height.label: Printable height
printable_height.tooltip: Maximum printable height which is limited by mechanism of printer.

support_multi_bed_types.label: Support multi bed types
support_multi_bed_types.tooltip: Enable this option if you want to use multiple bed types.

nozzle_volume.label: Nozzle volume
nozzle_volume.tooltip: Volume of nozzle between the cutter and the end of nozzle.

best_object_pos.label: Best object position
best_object_pos.tooltip: Best auto arranging position in range [0,1] w.r.t. bed shape.

z_offset.label: Z offset
z_offset.tooltip: This value will be added (or subtracted) from all the Z coordinates in the output G-code. It is used to compensate for bad Z endstop position: for example, if your endstop zero actually leaves the nozzle 0.3mm far from the print bed, set this to -0.3 (or fix your endstop).

preferred_orientation.label: Preferred orientation
preferred_orientation.tooltip: Automatically orient stls on the Z axis upon initial import.

printer_structure.label: Printer structure
printer_structure.tooltip: The physical arrangement and components of a printing device.

gcode_flavor.label: G-code flavor
gcode_flavor.tooltip: What kind of G-code the printer is compatible with.

gcode_skip_config_block.label: Skip G-code config block
gcode_skip_config_block.tooltip: Do not write the CONFIG_BLOCK (slicer configuration key/value pairs) into the G-code file. This can help with printers whose firmware crashes when parsing these comment lines (e.g. Anycubic go-klipper). Note: the G-code file will no longer contain slicer settings, so importing it back into OrcaSlicer will not restore the configuration.

pellet_modded_printer.label: Pellet Modded Printer
pellet_modded_printer.tooltip: Enable this option if your printer uses pellets instead of filaments.

bbl_use_printhost.label: Use 3rd-party print host
bbl_use_printhost.tooltip: Allow controlling BambuLab's printer through 3rd party print hosts.

enable_power_loss_recovery.label: Power Loss Recovery
enable_power_loss_recovery.tooltip: Choose how to control power loss recovery. When set to Printer configuration, the slicer will not emit power loss recovery G-code and will leave the printer's configuration unchanged. Applicable to Bambu Lab or Marlin 2 firmware based printers.

disable_m73.label: Disable set remaining print time
disable_m73.tooltip: Disable generating of the M73: Set remaining print time in the final G-code.

thumbnails.label: G-code thumbnails
thumbnails.tooltip: Picture sizes to be stored into a .gcode and .sl1 / .sl1s files, in the following format: "XxY, XxY, ..."

use_relative_e_distances.label: Use relative E distances
use_relative_e_distances.tooltip: Relative extrusion is recommended when using "label_objects" option. Some extruders work better with this option unchecked (absolute extrusion mode). Wipe tower is only compatible with relative mode. It is recommended on most printers. Default is checked.

use_firmware_retraction.label: Use firmware retraction
use_firmware_retraction.tooltip: This experimental setting uses G10 and G11 commands to have the firmware handle the retraction. This is only supported in recent Marlin.

fan_kickstart.label: Fan kick-start time
fan_kickstart.tooltip:
Emit a max fan speed command for this amount of seconds before reducing to target speed to kick-start the cooling fan.
This is useful for fans where a low PWM/power may be insufficient to get the fan started spinning from a stop, or to get the fan up to speed faster.
Set to 0 to deactivate.

part_cooling_fan_min_pwm.label: Minimum non-zero part cooling fan speed
part_cooling_fan_min_pwm.tooltip:
Some part-cooling fans cannot start spinning when commanded below a certain PWM duty cycle. When set above 0, any non-zero part-cooling fan command will be raised to at least this percentage so the fan reliably starts. A fan command of 0 (fan off) is always honoured exactly. This clamp is applied after every other fan calculation (first-layer ramp, layer-time interpolation, overhang/bridge/support-interface/ironing overrides), so scaling still operates within the range [this value, 100%].
If your firmware already disables the fan below a threshold (for example Klipper's [fan] off_below: 0.10 shuts the fan off whenever the commanded duty cycle is below 10%), this option and the firmware threshold should ideally be set to the same value. Matching them (e.g. off_below: 0.10 in Klipper and 10% here) guarantees the slicer never emits a non-zero value that the firmware would silently drop, and the fan never receives a value below the one you know it can actually spool at.
Set to 0 to deactivate.

extruder_clearance_radius.label: Radius
extruder_clearance_radius.tooltip: Clearance radius around extruder. Used for collision avoidance in by-object printing.

extruder_clearance_max_radius.label: Max Radius
extruder_clearance_max_radius.tooltip: Max clearance radius around extruder. Used for collision avoidance in by-object printing.

extruder_clearance_dist_to_rod.label: Distance to rod
extruder_clearance_dist_to_rod.tooltip: Horizontal distance of the nozzle tip to the rod's farther edge. Used for collision avoidance in by-object printing.

extruder_clearance_height_to_rod.label: Height to rod
extruder_clearance_height_to_rod.tooltip: Distance of the nozzle tip to the lower rod. Used for collision avoidance in by-object printing.

extruder_clearance_height_to_lid.label: Height to lid
extruder_clearance_height_to_lid.tooltip: Distance of the nozzle tip to the lid. Used for collision avoidance in by-object printing.

bed_mesh_min.label: Bed mesh min
bed_mesh_min.tooltip: This option sets the min point for the allowed bed mesh area. Due to the probe's XY offset, most printers are unable to probe the entire bed. To ensure the probe point does not go outside the bed area, the minimum and maximum points of the bed mesh should be set appropriately. EdgeSlicer ensures that adaptive_bed_mesh_min/adaptive_bed_mesh_max values do not exceed these min/max points. This information can usually be obtained from your printer manufacturer. The default setting is (-99999, -99999), which means there are no limits, thus allowing probing across the entire bed.

bed_mesh_max.label: Bed mesh max
bed_mesh_max.tooltip: This option sets the max point for the allowed bed mesh area. Due to the probe's XY offset, most printers are unable to probe the entire bed. To ensure the probe point does not go outside the bed area, the minimum and maximum points of the bed mesh should be set appropriately. EdgeSlicer ensures that adaptive_bed_mesh_min/adaptive_bed_mesh_max values do not exceed these min/max points. This information can usually be obtained from your printer manufacturer. The default setting is (99999, 99999), which means there are no limits, thus allowing probing across the entire bed.

bed_mesh_probe_distance.label: Probe point distance
bed_mesh_probe_distance.tooltip: This option sets the preferred distance between probe points (grid size) for the X and Y directions, with the default being 50mm for both X and Y.

adaptive_bed_mesh_margin.label: Mesh margin
adaptive_bed_mesh_margin.tooltip: This option determines the additional distance by which the adaptive bed mesh area should be expanded in the XY directions.

nozzle_type.label: Nozzle type
nozzle_type.tooltip: The metallic material of nozzle. This determines the abrasive resistance of nozzle, and what kind of filament can be printed.

nozzle_hrc.label: Nozzle HRC
nozzle_hrc.tooltip: The nozzle's hardness. Zero means no checking for nozzle's hardness during slicing.

auxiliary_fan.label: Auxiliary part cooling fan
auxiliary_fan.tooltip: Enable this option if machine has auxiliary part cooling fan. G-code command: M106 P2 S(0-255).

support_chamber_temp_control.label: Support control chamber temperature
support_chamber_temp_control.tooltip:
This option is enabled if machine support controlling chamber temperature
G-code command: M141 S(0-255)

support_air_filtration.label: Support air filtration
support_air_filtration.tooltip:
Enable this if printer support air filtration
G-code command: M106 P3 S(0-255)

unload_filaments_at_end.label: Unload filaments after print
unload_filaments_at_end.tooltip: Ask the printer to unload the filaments this print used once it has finished (Snapmaker tool changers only). The printer does the unloading itself, at the end of its own PRINT_END routine, and skips any toolhead holding a flexible filament. This is sent with the print, so it only applies to prints started from this slicer. This is only the default: the Send G-code to printer host dialog can override it for a single print.

file_start_gcode.label: File header G-code
file_start_gcode.tooltip: G-code written at the very top of the output file, before any other content. Useful for adding metadata that printer firmware reads from the first lines of the file (e.g. estimated print time, filament usage). Supports placeholders like {print_time_total_sec}, {print_time_day}, {print_time_hour}, {print_time_minute}, {print_time_sec} and {used_filament_length}.

machine_start_gcode.label: Start G-code
machine_start_gcode.tooltip: Start G-code when starting the entire print.
machine_start_gcode.default:
G28 ; home all axes
G1 Z5 F5000 ; lift nozzle

machine_end_gcode.label: End G-code
machine_end_gcode.tooltip: End G-code when finishing the entire print.
machine_end_gcode.default:
M104 S0 ; turn off temperature
G28 X0  ; home X axis
M84     ; disable motors

printing_by_object_gcode.label: Between Object G-code
printing_by_object_gcode.tooltip: Insert G-code between objects. This parameter will only come into effect when you print your models object by object.

before_layer_change_gcode.label: Before layer change G-code
before_layer_change_gcode.tooltip: This G-code is inserted at every layer change before the Z lift.

layer_change_gcode.label: Layer change G-code
layer_change_gcode.tooltip: This G-code is inserted at every layer change after the Z lift.

change_filament_gcode.label: Change filament G-code
change_filament_gcode.tooltip: This G-code is inserted when filament is changed, including T commands to trigger tool change.

change_extrusion_role_gcode.label: Change extrusion role G-code
change_extrusion_role_gcode.tooltip: This G-code is inserted when the extrusion role is changed.

machine_pause_gcode.label: Pause G-code
machine_pause_gcode.tooltip: This G-code will be used as a code for the pause print. Users can insert pause G-code in the G-code viewer.

template_custom_gcode.label: Custom G-code
template_custom_gcode.tooltip: This G-code will be used as a custom code.

single_extruder_multi_material.label: Single Extruder Multi Material
single_extruder_multi_material.tooltip: Use single nozzle to print multi filament.

extruders_count.label: Extruders
extruders_count.tooltip: Number of extruders of the printer.

manual_filament_change.label: Manual Filament Change
manual_filament_change.tooltip: Enable this option to omit the custom Change filament G-code only at the beginning of the print. The tool change command (e.g., T0) will be skipped throughout the entire print. This is useful for manual multi-material printing, where we use M600/PAUSE to trigger the manual filament change action.

wipe_tower_type.label: Wipe tower type
wipe_tower_type.tooltip: Choose the wipe tower implementation for multi-material prints. Type 1 suits printers that cut the filament and purge the old one into the tower, as Bambu Lab printers do. Type 1 purges through your printer's change filament G-code (flush_length); if that G-code doesn't use it, only the prime volume is purged and there is no ramming. Type 2 suits MMU, ramming and tool-changer setups, and is the safe choice for most printers.

purge_in_prime_tower.label: Purge in prime tower
purge_in_prime_tower.tooltip: Purge remaining filament into prime tower.

tool_change_on_wipe_tower.label: Tool change on wipe tower
tool_change_on_wipe_tower.tooltip: Force the toolhead to travel to the wipe tower before issuing the tool change command (Tx). Only relevant for multi-extruder (multi-toolhead) printers using a Type 2 wipe tower. By default Orca skips the travel on multi-toolhead machines because the firmware handles the head swap, which can result in the Tx command being issued above the printed part. Enable this option if you want the tool change to always be issued above the wipe tower instead.

wait_for_temp_on_wipe_tower.label: Wait for temperature on wipe tower
wait_for_temp_on_wipe_tower.tooltip: Pick up the new tool without waiting for it to reach printing temperature, travel to the wipe tower, and wait for the temperature there, right before purging. Ooze from the heat-up lands on the tower instead of the model, and the travel overlaps with the heating. Only relevant for multi-extruder (multi-toolhead) printers using a Type 2 wipe tower. The firmware or tool change macro must not wait for the temperature itself. When disabled, the temperature wait is issued right after the tool change command.

ramming_line_width_ratio.label: Ramming line width ratio
ramming_line_width_ratio.tooltip: This is used to decide the line width of wipe tower when ramming, ramming line width = [this ratio] * extruder * 1.25

enable_change_pressure_when_wiping.label: Enable change pressure advance when wiping
enable_change_pressure_when_wiping.tooltip: If it's set to false, the pressure advance value will not be changed.

ramming_pressure_advance_value.label: Pressure advance value when ramming
ramming_pressure_advance_value.tooltip: Set_Pressure_advance [this value] when ramming on wipe tower

tool_slot_model.label: Per-tool process slots
tool_slot_model.tooltip: Experimental. The process keeps values per tool, flow type and nozzle diameter, and each filament reads the values of the nozzle it prints on.

support_filament_nozzle_mapping.label: Declare physical nozzles
support_filament_nozzle_mapping.tooltip: Experimental. Write the diameter and flow type of every physical nozzle into the G-code (physical_nozzle_properties) so the printer can check the fitted nozzles.

cooling_tube_retraction.label: Cooling tube position
cooling_tube_retraction.tooltip: Distance of the center-point of the cooling tube from the extruder tip.

cooling_tube_length.label: Cooling tube length
cooling_tube_length.tooltip: Length of the cooling tube to limit space for cooling moves inside it.

parking_pos_retraction.label: Filament parking position
parking_pos_retraction.tooltip: Distance of the extruder tip from the position where the filament is parked when unloaded. This should match the value in printer firmware.

extra_loading_move.label: Extra loading distance
extra_loading_move.tooltip: When set to zero, the distance the filament is moved from parking position during load is exactly the same as it was moved back during unload. When positive, it is loaded further, if negative, the loading move is shorter than unloading.

high_current_on_filament_swap.label: High extruder current on filament swap
high_current_on_filament_swap.tooltip: It may be beneficial to increase the extruder motor current during the filament exchange sequence to allow for rapid ramming feed rates and to overcome resistance when loading a filament with an ugly shaped tip.

machine_prepare_time.label: Prepare time
machine_prepare_time.tooltip: Fixed time added to the print time estimate to account for machine startup routines (homing, bed mesh, nozzle purge, etc.). Added once to the total; does not affect the sliced G-code.

machine_load_filament_time.label: Filament load time
machine_load_filament_time.tooltip: Time to load new filament when switch filament. It's usually applicable for single-extruder multi-material machines. For tool changers or multi-tool machines, it's typically 0. For statistics only.

machine_unload_filament_time.label: Filament unload time
machine_unload_filament_time.tooltip: Time to unload old filament when switch filament. It's usually applicable for single-extruder multi-material machines. For tool changers or multi-tool machines, it's typically 0. For statistics only.

machine_tool_change_time.label: Tool change time
machine_tool_change_time.tooltip: Time taken to switch tools. It's usually applicable for tool changers or multi-tool machines. For single-extruder multi-material machines, it's typically 0. For statistics only.

tool_change_temprature_wait.label: Wait for the temperature when changing tools
tool_change_temprature_wait.tooltip: It will use the M109 instead of M104 T[target] after changing tools if this is set to true

min_layer_height.label: Min
min_layer_height.tooltip: The lowest printable layer height for the extruder. Used to limit the minimum layer height when enable adaptive layer height.

max_layer_height.label: Max
max_layer_height.tooltip: The highest printable layer height for the extruder. Used to limit the maximum layer height when enable adaptive layer height.

retraction_length.label: Length
retraction_length.tooltip: Some amount of material in extruder is pulled back to avoid ooze during long travel. Set zero to disable retraction.

retract_restart_extra.label: Extra length on restart
retract_restart_extra.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after the travel move, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament. This setting is rarely needed.

retraction_speed.label: Retraction Speed
retraction_speed.tooltip: Speed for retracting filament from the nozzle.

deretraction_speed.label: De-retraction Speed
deretraction_speed.tooltip: Speed for reloading filament into the nozzle. Zero means same speed of retraction.

retraction_minimum_travel.label: Travel distance threshold
retraction_minimum_travel.tooltip: Only trigger retraction when the travel distance is longer than this threshold.

retract_when_changing_layer.label: Retract when change layer
retract_when_changing_layer.tooltip: Force a retraction when changes layer.

wipe.label: Wipe while retracting
wipe.tooltip: Move nozzle along the last extrusion path when retracting to clean any leaked material on the nozzle. This can minimize blobs when printing a new part after traveling.

wipe_distance.label: Wipe Distance
wipe_distance.tooltip:
Describe how long the nozzle will move along the last path when retracting.

Depending on how long the wipe operation lasts, how fast and long the extruder/filament retraction settings are, a retraction move may be needed to retract the remaining filament.

Setting a value in the retract amount before wipe setting below will perform any excess retraction before the wipe, else it will be performed after.

retract_before_wipe.label: Retract amount before wipe
retract_before_wipe.tooltip: The length of fast retraction before wipe, relative to retraction length.

retract_after_wipe.label: Retract amount after wipe
retract_after_wipe.tooltip:
The length of fast retraction after wipe, relative to retraction length.
The value will be clamped by 100% minus the retract amount before the wipe value.

retract_lift_enforce.label: On surfaces
retract_lift_enforce.tooltip: Enforce Z-Hop behavior. This setting is impacted by the above settings (Only lift Z above/below).

z_hop.label: Z-hop height
z_hop.tooltip: Whenever the retraction is done, the nozzle is lifted a little to create clearance between nozzle and the print. It prevents nozzle from hitting the print when travel move. Using spiral lines to lift Z can prevent stringing.

z_hop_when_prime.label: Z hop when moving to tower

travel_slope.label: Traveling angle
travel_slope.tooltip: Traveling angle for Slope and Spiral Z-hop type. Setting it to 90° results in Normal Lift.

retract_lift_above.label: Only lift Z above
retract_lift_above.tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place above the specified absolute Z.

retract_lift_below.label: Only lift Z below
retract_lift_below.tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place below the specified absolute Z.

retract_restart_extra_toolchange.label: Extra length on restart
retract_restart_extra_toolchange.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after changing tool, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament.

long_retractions_when_cut.label: Long retraction when cut (beta)
long_retractions_when_cut.tooltip: Experimental feature: Retracting and cutting off the filament at a longer distance during changes to minimize purge. While this reduces flush significantly, it may also raise the risk of nozzle clogs or other printing problems.

retraction_distances_when_cut.label: Retraction distance when cut
retraction_distances_when_cut.tooltip: Experimental feature: Retraction length before cutting off during filament change. Set zero to disable the long retraction.

emit_machine_limits_to_gcode.label: Emit limits to G-code
emit_machine_limits_to_gcode.tooltip:
If enabled, the machine limits will be emitted to G-code file.
This option will be ignored if the G-code flavor is set to Klipper.

resonance_avoidance.label: Resonance avoidance
resonance_avoidance.tooltip:
By reducing the speed of the outer wall to avoid the resonance zone of the printer, ringing on the surface of the model are avoided.
Please turn this option off when testing ringing.

input_shaping_emit.label: Emit input shaping
input_shaping_emit.tooltip:
Override firmware input shaping settings.
If disabled, firmware settings are used.

input_shaping_type.label: Input shaper type
input_shaping_type.tooltip:
Choose the input shaper algorithm.
Default uses the firmware default settings.
Disable turns off input shaping in the firmware.

input_shaping_freq_x.label: X
input_shaping_freq_x.tooltip:
Resonant frequency for the X axis input shaper.
Zero will use the firmware frequency.
To disable input shaping, use the Disable type.
RRF: X and Y values are equal.

input_shaping_freq_y.label: Y
input_shaping_freq_y.tooltip:
Resonant frequency for the Y axis input shaper.
Zero will use the firmware frequency.
To disable input shaping, use the Disable type.

input_shaping_damp_x.label: X
input_shaping_damp_x.tooltip:
Damping ratio for the X axis input shaper.
Zero will use the firmware damping ratio.
To disable input shaping, use the Disable type.
RRF: X and Y values are equal.

input_shaping_damp_y.label: Y
input_shaping_damp_y.tooltip:
Damping ratio for the Y axis input shaper.
Zero will use the firmware damping ratio.
To disable input shaping, use the Disable type.

machine_max_acceleration_x.label: Maximum acceleration X
machine_max_acceleration_x.tooltip: Maximum acceleration of the X axis

machine_max_acceleration_y.label: Maximum acceleration Y
machine_max_acceleration_y.tooltip: Maximum acceleration of the Y axis

machine_max_acceleration_z.label: Maximum acceleration Z
machine_max_acceleration_z.tooltip: Maximum acceleration of the Z axis

machine_max_acceleration_e.label: Maximum acceleration E
machine_max_acceleration_e.tooltip: Maximum acceleration of the E axis

machine_max_acceleration_travel.label: Maximum acceleration for travel
machine_max_acceleration_travel.tooltip: Maximum acceleration for travel (M204 T), it only applies to Marlin 2.

machine_max_junction_deviation.label: Maximum Junction Deviation
machine_max_junction_deviation.tooltip:
Maximum junction deviation (M205 J, only apply if JD > 0 for Marlin Firmware
If your Marlin 2 printer uses Classic Jerk set this value to 0.)

machine_max_jerk_x.label: Maximum jerk X
machine_max_jerk_x.tooltip: Maximum jerk of the X axis

machine_max_jerk_y.label: Maximum jerk Y
machine_max_jerk_y.tooltip: Maximum jerk of the Y axis

machine_max_jerk_z.label: Maximum jerk Z
machine_max_jerk_z.tooltip: Maximum jerk of the Z axis

machine_max_jerk_e.label: Maximum jerk E
machine_max_jerk_e.tooltip: Maximum jerk of the E axis

printer_notes.label: Printer notes
printer_notes.tooltip: You can put your notes regarding the printer here.
